text: Hɔɔlɩŋ cikpeŋ ñɩɩ ñɩɩ kpɛndʋʋna nɛ pɩ-la kpɩna tomnasɩ. A-tɔkɩ tɔɔnasɩ nɛ sɩ-yɔlʋʋ a-taa. Kpɩna sakɩyɛ pɩzɩɣ a-kɛɛ lona.
text_en: Animals are made of many cells. They eat things and digest them inside. Most animals can move.

text: Kpɩna ɖeke wɛnɩna fɩtɩɩlɩm / feteenim (ɛlɛ pɩ-tɛkɛ a-tɩŋgɛ a-wɛnɩna; ɖɩ-kpaɣnɩ zɩɩ kpakpasi nasɩyɩ, sɩ-fɛɩnɩ fɩtɩɩlɩm).
text_en: Only animals have brains (though not even all animals do; jellyfish, for example, do not have brains).

text: Ɖɩnaɣ kpɩnaa kedeŋga yɔɔ paa le. A-huyuu tataa, a-yaɣ lɩmm limwadaɣ taa, nɛ a-kʋyʋ ɛsɔ taa.
text_en: Animals are found all over the earth. They dig in the ground, swim in the oceans, and fly in the sky.

text: tomnaɣ hɔɔlaɣ kɛnɩ tomnaɣ egbeliye cikpeɖe kpaagba nɖɛ nɖɩ ɖɩ-wɛnɩ wezuu yɔ. Nɖɩɩ pa-yaɣnɩ anglisi taa se ''sell''.
text_en: A cell is the smallest structural and functional unit of a living (things) organism.

text: Pa-kindɩ Cell kɛ Latɛ tomiye sella taa nɩ pa-nɩɣ ɖɩ-taa se ɖaŋ cikpeluu.
text_en: Cell comes from the Latin word cella which means small room.

text: Yee ɛyʋ ɛ-cɔŋnɩ wezuu wonduu lɔŋ ɛsɛñɩnɩŋ tɛɛ kɛyɔɔ, n'naɣ se pʋ-wɛɛ zɩɩ cacabe hɔɔlʋ yaa malɩfabɛ manɩ-dʋ.
text_en: If you look at living things under a microscope, you will see that they are made of small squares or balls.

text: Robert Hooke, England tɛ lɔŋñɩnʋ taa cɔnɩyʋ, na tɔm maʋ kpatanaa ñɩɩ ñɩɩ waa kɛ lɔŋñɩnɩʋ taa.
text_en: Robert Hooke, a biologist from England, saw small squares in cork with a microscope.

text: Paawɛɛ ɛzɩ ɖamɩŋ yɔ. Ɛnʋʋ lɛ kajalaɣ-dʋ weyi ɛ-na sim tomnaɣ egbeela yɔ.
text_en: They looked like rooms. He was the first person to observe dead cells

text: Wondu  nɛ tɩ-tambɔɔ pa-pɩzɩɣ pɔ-kpɔ wɛtʋ ndɩ ndɩ kɛ masɩ kɩɩ-lɛɛzʋʋ taa.
text_en: Elements and compounds can move from one state to another and not change.

text: Heelim mbʋ ansaaɩ ya-bʋ se niitorozɛɛnɩ yɔ, lɩm nitorozɛɛnɩ masɩ ɖʋɖɔɔ pʋ-wɛna. Pɩ-tɛ lɩm wɛtʋ lɩʋ ɛsɛ yɔɔ pɩkpaɖɩ ɛlɛ pɩ-tambɔɔ kaɣʋ kɛ kʋɖʋmam.
text_en: Nitrogen as a gas still has the same properties as liquid nitrogen. The liquid state is denser but the molecules are still the same.

text: Lɩm kɛnɩ kpaɣnaʋ zɩɩ lɛɛbʋ. Lɩm mayaɣ taa lɛ ɖɩ-naɣ ansaayɩ taa idorozɛɛnɩ tambɔɔ naalɛ nɛ heelim taa wezuu ñɩm mbʋ ansayɩ yaa se ɔksiizɛɛnɩ yɔ pɩ-tambɔɔyɛ kʋɖʋmɖɛɛ.
text_en: Water is another example. The compound water is made up of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

text: Pʋwɛnɩ tambɔɔ tɩnʋʋ kʋɖʋmam paa pɩɩ-kɛnɩ heelim, lɩm, yaa kpendelim.
text_en: It has the same molecular structure whether it is a gas, liquid, or solid.

text: Toovenim se ɛsɛ yɔɔ masɩ pɩzʋʋ sɩ-lɛɛzɩ, ɛlɛ pɩ-taa masɩ wɛ si-ɖeɖe.
text_en: Although its physical state may change, its chemical state remains the same.

text: Alɩwaatʋ kɛnɩ nabʋyʋ mbʋ pʋjɔ-ɖʋ nɛ pɩta yɔ, nɛ pɩ-taɣkʋʋna mbʋ pɩ-dɩŋgɛ ɖɩ-lakɩ yɔ, kɛlɛnɩ pɩtɛɛ nɩʋ wɛ kaɖɛ.
text_en: Time is something that is all around us, and affects everything we do, yet is difficult to understand.

text: Pɩnzɩ kutokiŋ cabɩ kɛyɔ, tɩlɩyaa Ɛsɔ kɩlaʋ taa, lɩmaɣza lɩzʋʋ nʋmʋʋ taa nɛ sukuli kɩtɛɛzʋʋ taa mba kpɛlɩkaa nɛ pa-tazɩ  alɩwaatʋ tɔm taa.
text_en: Time has been studied by religious, philosophical, and scientific scholars for thousands of years.

text: Ɖɩkpɛlɩkɩ alɩwaatʋ nɛ tʋ-sʋʋna-ɖʋ ɛzɩɩ mbʋ mbʋ pɩ-lakɩ ɛjɛɖɛ yɔɔ, kpaɣna mbʋ pʋ-kɔŋ yɔ, mbʋ pʋ-ɖɔŋ labʋ yɔ nɛ mbʋ pɩ-tɛmɩ ɖɛʋ yɔ pʋ-yɔɔ
text_en: We experience time as a series of events passing from the future through the present to the past.

text: Alʋwaatʋ kɛnɩ ɖʋɖɔɔ ɛzɩma ɖɩ-maɣzʋʋ mbʋ pɩ-lakɩ ɖe-wezuu caɣʋ taa yɔ pɩ-tɛ ɖaɣlɩkɩŋ yaa pɩtɛ leɖuu.
text_en: Time is also how we compare the duration (length) of events.

text: Ñɛ maɣmaɣ m-pɩzɩɣ ŋ-maɣzɩ alɩwaatʋ kɛ ŋ-kɔcɔŋna mbʋ pɩ-lakɩ yɔ pɩ-tɛm nɛ pɩ-baazʋʋ. Mbʋ pɩ-lakɩ yɔ pɩ-kɛnɩ nabʋyʋ mbʋ pɩ-tɛŋ nɛ pɩ-paɣzʋʋ ɖamayɔɔ ɖamayɔɔ yɔ.
text_en: You can mark the passing of time yourself by observing the repetition of a cyclical event. A cyclical event is something that happens again and again regularly.

text: Sɔnɔ kɩdaʋ kʋnɛ yɔ, pɑ-kpakʋʋ ɔrdinatɛɛrɩnaa nɛ pɛ-lɛɛzɩɣna kɩlɛmɩŋ weyi ii-ciɣdiɣ nɛ pa-yaa-ɩ se footonaa yɔ, nɛ i-ciɣdiɣ nɛ pa-yaa-ɩ se fiilimnaa yaa fideonaa yɔ.
text_en: Computers today are used to manipulate pictures and videos.

text: Pa-pɩzɩɣ pa-kpa ciɣdiɣ kɩlɛmɩŋ siŋŋ siŋŋwaa kɛ ɔrdinatɛɛrɩnaa yɔɔ, kɛyɔ pɩ-tɛ kɩlɛmɩŋ kɛ pa-kɩlɩɣ lɩzɩɣ llɛɛlɛyɔ kɛ televisɔŋnaa nɛ filimnaa taa
text_en: Sophisticated animations can be constructed on computers, and this kind of animation is increasingly being used in television and films.

text: Ɔrdiinatɛɛrɩnaa siŋŋ siŋŋwaa kɛ pa-gbaɣna miziki nɛ pe-sidiɣna nɛ pɛ-kpɛndʋʋ hendu.
text_en: Music is often recorded using sophisticated computers to process and mix sounds together.

text: Canawu ɛsi waasɩ niidozo nɛ loɖo ŋgbaɣ ŋwolo nɩɩnaza mbʋyɔ lɛ, paɣmaɣzaɣ se New Zealand ɛjaɖɛ kaɣnaɣ mba lɛ Maori caŋga taa mba, mba kʋwaynaɣ simasɩ sʋsɔsɩ ŋzi paɣyaɣwaɣ moas wa yɔ.
text_en: For a long time during the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, it was believed the first inhabitants of New Zealand were the Maori people, who hunted giant birds called moas.

text: Lmayziɛ kɔmɩ plɩnɩ wayɩ wayɩ se Maoria mba lɩna Polinesia lim yɔ lɔɖɩ sɔssɔɖɛ naɖɩ taa kɔnɛ yɔ nɛ pɔɖɔnɩ caʋ New Zealand ŋwolo ŋzini Moriori nɛ pɛkɛnɩ haɖaa gɛɛ peye.
text_en: The theory then established the idea that the Maori people migrated from Polynesia in a Great Fleet and took New Zealand from the Moriori, establishing an agricultural society.

text: Paa pdɩwɛ ŋna yɔ, asere tom natɩyu wɩlu se Maoria mba kɛnɩ Maori ɛjaɖɛ taa ɛya caŋga ŋga kalɩni Niyuu Zelandɩ ɛjaɖɛ daa nɛ ɖwolo Chatmania hɔlɩŋ weyi ɛwɛ lɩm daa yɔ, peye paɖʋ pewezu cawʋ nɛ dɩdɩɣ caɣu paa
text_en: However, new evidence suggests that the Moriori were a group of mainland Maori who migrated from New Zealand to the Chatham Islands, developing their own distinctive, peaceful culture.

text: Ɛya nabaya katɛmɩwɛu Chathamania hɔliŋ taá nɛ pkenɩ Maori mbà mbá palɩnɩ New Zealand yɔ
text_en: There was also another tribe on the Chatham islands these were Maori who migrated away from New Zealand.

text: Paya padi hɩdɛ se Moriori mba nɛ pkonɩ nɔhɔŋɖɛ, nɛ pakʋ Moriori mba.
text_en: They called themselves the Moriori there were a few skirmishes and in the end, the Moriori were wiped out

text: Ɛya mba pdaɣnɩ bɛ ɖoo waasɩ nɛ waasɩ yɔ, pasɩnaɖʋ nɛ samtʋ nɛ ayɩɣya ɖoɖoŋ nɛ ɖatʋmiɛ labʋ ptɛ lɛ, peheyiɖʋ petevenim plina mbu pɛɛsɛ naɣ ɖɛjɛyitʋ nɛ ɖɛgɛgbɛtɛsasɩ yɔɔ yɔ.
text_en: Individuals who had been involved for several decades helped us appreciate our strengths and passions while candidly assessing difficulties and even failures.

text: Ŋnɩ ɛya gɛdɩɣ pohɔŋ nɛ patʋmɛ taa tom yɔ, ŋnaɣ ɛzɩma nabaya wezou caɣu kpaziɣ yaa rʋzʋ ŋgbɛ yɔ.
text_en: While listening to individuals share their individual, family, and organizational stories, we gained valuable insight into the past and some of the personalities who influenced for good or ill the culture of the organization.

text: Ɛyɔ wezu caɣu tɩlʋ ɩyekna se ŋdɩlɩ ɛdɛ sɔŋzi, paa nɛ ɛzɩma yɔ pyekɩ nɛ ɛya tlɩ polonie ŋgbɛ taa.
text_en: While understanding one’s history does not assume understanding of culture, it does at least help people gain a sense of where they fall within the history of the organization.

text: Pɩŋna ɛssɩŋda wobu nɛ wayi pisʋ yɔɔ lɛ, ɛya yem wa hiku nɛ patlɩ pɛŋgbɛ dɛ camiɛ laɣsɩ, ɖtʋma, nɛ mbu ɖgaɖɩɣna yɔ.
text_en: While assessing the successes and becoming aware of failures, individuals and the whole of the participating persons discover more deeply the values, mission, and driving forces of the organization.

text: Pwɛ cinɛ yɔ, ti-yɔ tʋmɩyɛ labʋ tɛ wɛtʋ nɛ ɛzima pwonɩ ɛya nɛ esɩŋda yɔ, pzinɩ pdɩfɛyɩ nɛ patisɩ pamʋ wɛtʋ kfatʋ nɛ lmaɣza kfana plina pɛdɛ cɔcɩ nɔmɔu taa.
text_en: In this instance, recalling previous instances of entrepreneurial behavior and resulting successes helped people to be open to new changes and new direction for the local church.

text: Ɛyaa mba papɩza nɛ powobɩna ɛsɩnda yɔ, pɛdɛ wezu caʋ tɔm pazɩ lɛzʋ sɔndu pɩdɩfɛyɩ, pɩtɛ nɛ pɩsɔsʋʋ tiluzu  kɩfam ɛsɩndaa ɖɛnɑʋ yɔɔ
text_en: Such success stories lessened the fears of change, while creating positive inclinations toward change in the future.

text: Lɩmaɣza kpɛndʋʋ nʋmɔŋ kɛnɩ tɔm ñɔɔzʋʋ lɛɣtʋ nʋmɔŋ weyi ɩkpɛndɩɣ lɩmaɣza ndɩ ndɩ yaa hɔɔlɩŋ ndɩ ndɩ tɔm se pɩsa pehiɣ nʋmɔʋ kɩbaŋʋ nɛ pɔcɔnɩ tɔm natʋyʋ ɖeɖe yɔ.
text_en: Convergent thinking patterns are problem solving techniques that unite different ideas or fields to find a solution.

text: Lɩmaɣza ana a-wɛnʋʋ pɔzʋʋ se ɛyʋ ɛmaɣzɩɣ lɛɛ lɛɛ, ɛcɔlʋʋ lɩmaɣza camɩyɛ nɛ atʋʋzɩ, pɩtasɩ lɛ ɛtɩlɩ mba pɩlaba ɖeyi ɖeyi yɔ, ɛɖaɣnɩ labɩnʋʋ tʋmɩyɛ lɛɣtʋ kɩbɩndʋ, ekpeɣli tɔm.
text_en: The focus of this mindset is speed, logic and accuracy, also identification of facts, reapplying existing techniques, gathering information.

text: Tɔm kɩcɛyɩtʋ ndʋ pɩwɛɛ se ɛyʋ ɛtɩlɩ lɩmaɣza ana a-wɛnʋʋ taa yɔ lɛ se : tɔm cosuu kɩbambʋ kʋɖʋm wɛnaa. Pɩwɛɛ se ŋmaɣzɩ tɔm cosuu naalɛ yeke yɔɔ na, pʋ-tɔbʋʋ pɩwɛ ɖeu yaa pɩfɛyɩ ɖeu.
text_en: The most important factor of this mindset is: there is only one correct answer. You only think of two answers, namely right or wrong.

text: Lɩmaɣza ana a-wɛnʋʋ lɩɣnɩ lɛɣtʋ nʋmɔŋ nɛ tʋmɩyɛ labʋ ɖʋtʋ natʋyʋ cɔlɔ na.
text_en: This type of thinking is associated with certain science or standard procedures.

text: Ɛyaa mba pɛwɛnɩ lɩmaɣza ana yɔ, pamaɣzɩɣ nɛ pɩcɔlʋʋ camɩyɛ, papɩzɩɣ pɔɖɔkɩ tɔm sakɩyɛ, pɔcɔnɩ tɩlasɩ ndɩ ndɩ ɖeɖe nɛ pala lɛɣtʋ santaɖaʋnaa ndɩ ndɩ.
text_en: People with this type of thinking have logical thinking, are able to memorize patterns, solve problems and work on scientific tests.

text: Eyaa ɖeke kɛnɩ kpɩna wena akɩlɩ kpekpeka lɛlaa lɩmaɣza taa cɔnaʋ.
text_en: Humans are by far the most talented species in reading the minds of others.

text: Pʋtɔbʋ se ɖɩwɛnɩ waɖɛ se ɖɩmaɣsɩ, ɖɩkpeɣ, ɖɩtɩsɩ nɛ ɖɩtɩlɩ lɛlaa tɛ lɩmaɣzɛɛ taa.
text_en: That means we are able to successfully predict what other humans perceive, intend, believe, know or desire.

text: Kpekpeka ndi ndi taa lɛ, ɛyaa lɛlaa nɩʋ wɛ wazaɣ pɩtfɛyɩ. Pɩsɩ-nɩ ɖʋ se ɖɩñɔɔsɩ tɛyʋ mbʋ pɩpɩsɩ pɩwɛ hɛkʋ taa pɩlɩna lakasɩ nzɩ sɩhaɣ youu yɔ.
text_en: Among these abilities, understanding the intention of others is crucial. It allows us to resolve possible ambiguities of physical actions.

text: Kpaɣ ɛzɩ yee ŋna nɔɔyʋ ɛwɛ ɛyɔkʋʋ lɛlʋ lɔrɩyɛ ñɩlʋʋ, ŋpɩsɩɣ ŋmaɣsɩ se ɛcaɣɑɣ se ɛ-mɩlɩ ɛ-lɔrɩyɛ.
text_en: For example, if you were to see someone breaking a car window, you would probably assume he was trying to steal a stranger’s car.

text: Pɩpɔsʋ se ɛ-tɔm hʋʋ ɛwɛ ndɩ ye elesi ɛ-lɔrɩyɛ ñɩma nɛ pɩke se ɛ-maɣmaɣ ɛ-lɔrɩyɛ ɛwɛ ɛyɔkʋʋ se ɛtʋlɩ.
text_en: He would need to be judged differently if he had lost his car keys and it was his own car that he was trying to break into.

text: MRI kɛna wɛtʋ ndʋ tɩyeki paɣmaɣsɩ sɛʋ mbʋ pɩke cɩkpem (NMR) ndʋ Felix Botch (ɛlaɣkaɣ tʋmɩyɛ Standford sukuli kɩtɛzʋ taa)na pɩŋsɩ 1930 waa taa nɛ Edward Purcell (Harvard sukuli kɩtɛzʋ taa.
text_en: MRI is based on a physics phenomenon called nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), which was discovered in the 1930s by Felix Bloch (working at Stanford University) and Edward Purcell (from Harvard University).

text: Sɛʋ mbʋ pɩtaa lɛ, nimasɩ fɛyɩ tɛ sɛʋ pɩhaɣ-na radio waɖɛ se pɩna radio tɛ yʋsasɩ cɩkpesɩ.
text_en: In this resonance, magnetic field and radio waves cause atoms to give off tiny radio signals.

text: Pɩnaɣ 1970 taa lɛ, Raymond Damadian ɖɔkɩta nɛ lɛɣtʋ cayʋʋ ñɩnaa nɛ ɛna kɛlɛm kɛlɛm sɛʋ kɩɖe.
text_en: In the year 1970, Raymond Damadian, a medical doctor and research scientist, discovered the basis for using magnetic resonance imaging as a tool for medical diagnosis.

text: Pɩŋsɩ naŋza wayɩ lɛ,  pɩha waɖɛ kɩfaɖɛ kedeŋ kpekpe taa pɩlɩna MRI yɔ.
text_en: Four years later a patent was granted, which was the world's first patent issued in the field of MRI.

text: Pɩnaɣ 1977 taa Dr Damadian tɛma ñɩyʋ ,ngʋ kɩnaɣ ɛyʋ tomnaɣ kpekpe taa mbʋ pɩɖɔŋ yɔ maʋ nɛ ɛpɩsɩ ɛyaa-kʋ se "Paawakɩm kaʋ".
text_en: In 1977, Dr. Damadian completed the construction of the first “whole-body” MRI scanner, which he called the ”Indomitable”.

text: Papɩsɩ ɖɔɖɔ se padʋ se paa weyi ɛsɔlaa yɔ ɛ-pɩsɩɣ nɛ ɛkɔ ɛla tʋmɩyɛ alɩwatʋ ndʋ ɛsɔla yɔ ansayɩ ñɩtʋ ƴɔ.
text_en: Asynchronous communication encourages time for reflection and reaction to others.

text: Pɩsɩŋna sukuli piyaa se sɩ-kpɛlɩkɩ alɩwatʋ ndʋ sɩsɔlaa yɔ nɛ ɛsɩna mbʋ sɩ-pɩsɩɣ yɔ pɩlɩna paɣtʋ ndʋ paɖʋwa yɔ tɩyɔɔ.
text_en: It allows students the ability to work at their own pace and control the pace of instructional information.

text: Ɖɔɖɔ lɛ, cɛyɩtʋ tɩɖɔ pɩlɩna alɩwatʋ ndʋ paɣhaɣ yɔ nɛ waɖɛ wɛ pɩlɩna alɩwatʋ ndʋ pa weyɩ ɛsɔla se ɛla tvɲɩyɛ (Bremer, 1998).
text_en: In addition, there are fewer time restrictions with the possibility of flexible working hours. (Bremer, 1998)

text: Intɛrnɛtɩ nɛ maɣyaɣ World Wide Web siɣna sukuli piyaa se sɩpɩsɩ sɩla mbʋ sɩñɩnɩɣ yɔ paa alɩwatʋ nɖʋ.
text_en: The use of the Internet and the World Wide Web allows learners to have access to information at all times.

text: Sukuli piyaa pɩsɩɣ ɖɔɖɔ se sɩ-cɛlɛ tʋmɩƴɛ ŋɖɩ sɩ-wɩlɩyaa pɔsɩ-sɩ yɔ paa alɩwatʋ evemiƴe taa nɛ sɩɖaŋ se pocosɩ sɩ lɔŋ, waɖɛ nɖɛ pɛfɛyɩna yɔ yee pike se powoki sukuli taa nɛ pan,i pa-wɩlɩyaa pakatɩ.
text_en: Students can also submit questions to instructors at any time of day and expect reasonably quick responses, rather than waiting until the next face-to-face meeting.

text: Kaɣnaɣ kpɛlɩkʋ haɣ waɖɛ se paa weyɩ ɛwɛ pɛyɛ taa. Kpɛlɩkʋ wɛ ndi ndi.
text_en: The postmodern approach to learning offers the freedom from absolutes. There is no one good way to learn.

text: Mbʋ pɩwɛ lɛ se pɩteke wonuu kʋyʋmʋʋ ɛyʋ kpɛlɛkɩ. Kpɛlɛkʋ wɛtʋ lɩna weyi ɛkpɛlɩkɩ yɔɔ ɛcɔlɔ nɛ mbʋ ɛkpɛlɩkɩ yɔɔ pɩyɔɔ.
text_en: In fact, there is not one good thing to learn.Learning takes place in the experience between the learner and the knowledge presented.

text: Kaɣnaɣ tɛ tɩlɩtʋ nɛ la pɩtɩnɛ ñe-ɖeke nɛ tɔm wɩlɩʋ, kpɛlɩkʋʋ nɛ tele yɔɔ lɩsɩɣ tɔm tɩnɛ tɩtɛ aseɖe.
text_en: Our current experience with all the do-it-yourself and information presenting, learning-based television shows illustrates this point.

text: ̃̃Ɖataa sakɩyɛ cɔna mbʋ mbʋ palakɩ tele taa ɖenɖe pɛkpɛlɩkɩɣ ɛyaa ɛsɩna palakɩ yaa lɛlaa lɔŋsɩɖɛ ɛlɛ ɖɩkaɣ cɔsuu yaa ɖɩkaɣ labɩnaʋ tʋmɩyɛ kaʋ.
text_en: So many of us find ourselves watching a television show that informs us of a process or experience in which we will never participate or apply that knowledge.

text: Ɖɩpɩsɩ se ɖɩɖaɣnɩ lɔrɩƴɛ ñɔzʋʋ, ɖʋɖʋ pɔmpɩ ɖɛ wayɩ, ɖɩɖɔ nɩmɔʋ se ɖɩwolo Peru tɛtʋ taa se ɖɩcɔna ŋcɛƴɛ ya ɖɩɖaɣ ɖɔcɔlɔ ñɩma ɖɛ ñɔzʋʋ.
text_en: We will never overhaul a car, build a fountain in our backyard, travel to Peru to examine ancient ruins, or remodel our neighbour's house.

text: Pɩlɩna lɩm tɛ nɩmaɣ yɔɔ lɛ, ansayɩna tɛtʋ nɛ tɛtʋ nɖʋ pɔñɔsɩ tɩŋ nɛ caɣmaɣ tɩtamaa nɛ ajɛɛ ana a-taa ñɩma wɛna internentɩ  93%.
text_en: Thanks to undersea fiber optic cable links to Europe and broadband satellite, Greenland is well connected with 93% of the population having internet access.

text: Ŋɛ tɛ agɔmaa  ɖɛ yaa ɖenɖe ɛyaa mʋŋ yɔ (ye ŋcakɩ agɔmaa ɖɛ yaa nɔyʋ ɖɛ taa) wɛna wifi yaa internetɩ ñɩyʋ yɔ nɛ lona ndi ndi wɛna internetɩ yaa wifi ŋgʋ samaɣ pɩsɩɣ kowolo se kala tʋmɩyɛ yɔ.
text_en: Your hotel or hosts (if staying in a guesthouse or private home) will likely have wifi or an internet connected PC, and all settlements have an internet cafe or some location with public wifi.

text: Ɛzɩ ɖɩyɔɔdʋʋ nɛ pɩɖɛɛ yɔ, paa pɩɩcɛyɩɣ ɛyaa se palabɩnɩ tʋmɩyɛ tɔm piye « Eskimo » Etaazuuni ɛjaɖɛ taa yɔ, pɩɩkɛdɩɣnɩ Arkitiki mba kɔzɩ kɔzɩ mba pɛwɛ Kanadaa yɔ se payaa-wɛ nɛ hɩɖɛ nɖɩ.
text_en: As mentioned above, though the word "Eskimo" remains acceptable in the United States, it is considered pejorative by many non-U.S. Arctic peoples, especially in Canada.

text: Pʋtɔma yɔ ŋpɩzɩɣ nɛ ŋnɩɩ tɔm piye nɖɩ Greeland mba nɔsɩ taa, ɛlɛ pɩtɩpɔzɩ se agɔma ɩlabɩnɩ tɔm piye nɖɩ tʋmɩyɛ
text_en: While you may hear the word used by Greenlandic Natives, its use should be avoided by foreigners.

text: Greeland tɛtʋ taa mba yaɣ pa-tɩ se Inuyiti Kanada ɛjaɖɛ taa nɛ kalaalɛɛkɩ (pɔɖɔwa yɔ Kalaaliiti), pʋ-tɔbʋʋ se Greeland tɛtʋ taa tʋ Greeland ɛjaɖɛ taa.
text_en: The native inhabitants of Greenland call themselves Inuit in Canada and Kalaalleq (plural Kalaallit), a Greenlander, in Greenland.

text: Agɔma kañtʋ labʋ nɛ pɔyɔ kʋyʋ tɔm fɛɩ Greenland ɛjarɛ taa. Paa tɛtʋ taa maɣmaɣ kɛyɔ, ɖelɩ nɔyu fɛyɩnɩ kɩdɛkɛdɩm lakassɩ.
text_en: Crime, and ill-will toward foreigners in general, is virtually unknown in Greenland. Even in the towns, there are no "rough areas."

text: Nɩkaɣ ɖeke kabɩsɩna kɛkɛni cɛyɩtʋ mba pɔñɔzɩ padɩ yɔ.
text_en: Cold weather is perhaps the only real danger the unprepared will face.

text: Yee nɩkaɣ taa ɛwoki Greenland ɛjaɖɛ taa yɔ ( ɛtɩlɩ sɩ nɩkaɣ wɛ pɩdɩfɛyɩ ɛjaɖɛ nɛ ɖidɛ hayo kiŋ), pɩgɛnɩ kɩjɛyʋ se ɛɖɔkɩ nɩkaɣ tokonaa sakɩyɛ.
text_en: If you visit Greenland during cold seasons (considering that the further north you go, the colder it will be), it is essential to bring warm enough clothing.

text: Kɩyakɩŋ weyɩ ɛwɛnɩ lʋŋgʋyɛ tɛ wɛtʋ nɩ pɖɔɔ yɔ, ɛpɩsaɣ ɛkonɩ cɛyɩtʋ pɩcɛlɩnɩ ɖom yaa tɔnʋ daa alafɩa.
text_en: The very long days in the summer can lead to problems getting sufficient sleep and associated health issues.

text: Ɛ-kpa mɩdɩ nɛ hayo kiŋ pɔtʋʋ soŋaɣ tɛ alɩwaatʋ taa. Paa tɩɩɖɛɛzɩɣ kʋdɔŋ nakʋyʋ yɔ, tɩpɩzʋʋ tɩcɛyʋʋ ɛyaa
text_en: During the summer, also watch out for the Nordic mosquitoes. Although they do not transmit any diseases, they can be irritating.

text: Alɩwatʋ ndʋ San Francisco tadɩyɛ nyɔtɩna kɩtɛ ɛsindaa ɖɛnaʋ pɩlɩɩna aleɣya nʋmɔʋ wobu, kɩtɛ tadɩyɛ wɛ ndɩ ndɩ.
text_en: While San Francisco's economy is linked to it being a world-class tourist attraction, its economy is diversified.

text: Tʋmɩyɛ ñɩnʋ hɔlɩŋ weyi ɛtaa tʋmɩyɛ wɛ sakɩyɛ lɛ tʋmɩyɛ siɣ siɣ ñɩma, komina, nesi tɛ liidiye tʋmɩyɛ, tadɩyɛ, nɛ aleɣya nʋmɔʋ wobu.
text_en: The largest employment sectors are professional services, government, finance, trade, and tourism.

text: Ɛtɛ tɔyʋʋ minziiki taa, filim waa taa, takayɩsɩ maʋ taa nɛ ɛzakuliye sɔsɔyɛ haa waɖɛ nɛ ɛyaa sɩɩ ɛ-ɛjaɖɛ nɛ ɖɩtɛ canaʋ wondu kedeŋa kpekpe yɔɔ yɔ
text_en: Its frequent portrayal in music, films, literature and popular culture has helped make the city and its landmarks known throughout the world.

text: San Francisko ɛjaɖɛ ma aleɣya nʋmɔʋ wobu akɔmaa ɖɛsɩ sɩsɔsɩ nɛ cikpesi sakɩyɛ
text_en: San Francisco has developed a large tourist infrastructure with numerous hotels, restaurants, and top-notch convention facilities.

text: San Francisko kɛni ɛjaɖɛ hɔlʋ taa déŋdé ɛzi mpiziɣ ni ŋdɔɔ Asia tɔnaɣsi lɛsi yɔ: ɛzi Korea, Thailand, India ni Japon ajɛya tɔnɔsi
text_en: San Francisco is also one of the best places in the nation for other Asian cuisine: Korean, Thai, Indian, and Japanese.

text: Walt Disney ɛjaɖɛ taa wobu wɩlɩ nʋmɔʋ sʋsɔʋ wobu pɩcɛlɩ na Amerika hɔŋ.
text_en: Traveling to Walt Disney World represents a major pilgrimage for many American families.

text: Eyaa tɛ wobu "sɩsɩɣ" wɩlɩɣ Orlando ɛsɔdaa lɔɖɩyɛ kpaɣʋ nɛ kadaɣ sʋsaɣ taa tɩbʋ, tʋmɩyɛ labʋ Disney agɔmaa ɖɛ, alɩwaatʋ lesʋʋ pɩtala kpɩtaɣʋ Disney tɛtʋ taa nɛ ɖɛ pɩsɩʋ lakɩ kaɖɛ.
text_en: The "typical" visit involves flying into Orlando International Airport, busing to an on-site Disney hotel, spending about a week without leaving Disney property, and returning home.

text: Pɔyɔɔdʊʊ "Disney Ɛjaɖɛ taa" wobu lɛ, ɛyaa maɣzʋʋ se tʋmaa ana a-ɖeke palakɩ peeɖe ɛlɛ tʋmaa ndɩ ndɩ sakɩyɛ wɛɛ nɩ palakɩ peeɖe
text_en: There are infinite variations possible, but this remains what most people mean when they talk of "going to Disney World".

text: Tikenaa mba paapɛdɩ sakɩyɛ kaŋgalaafunaa yɔɔ pɩtɩŋna anasaayɩ ñɩɩtʊ kɛlɛm kɛlɛm waa yɔɔ ɛzɩ eBay yaa Craigslist. Tikenaa mba pasʋʋnɩ wɛ kadaɣ ŋga palakɩnɩ kɛ tʋmɩyɛ cabɩ taa yɔɔ kɩyakɩŋ sakɩyɛ
text_en: Many tickets sold online through auction websites such as eBay or Craigslist are partially used multi-day park-hopper tickets.

text: Pɩkee tʋmɩyɛ nɖɛ ɖɩtɔyaa samaɣ taa ɛlɛ pɩtɩha nʋmɔʋ Disney egetiye taa: papɩsɩ pɛɖɛsɩ tikee naa mba.
text_en: While this is a very common activity, it is prohibited by Disney: the tickets are non-transferable.

text: Ye nɔɔyʋ ɛñɩnɩɣ se esiɣ kizinziku Grand Canyon (Kajalaŋa Sɔsɔɔ) nɔɔ yɔ kɔyɔ, pʋpɔzʋʋ se paha-ɩ takayaɣ ŋga kahaɣ-ɩ nʋmɔʋ yɔ.
text_en: Any camping below the rim in Grand Canyon requires a backcountry permit.

text: Pañɩnɩɣ se pakandɩyɩ kajalaŋa yɔɔ pʋyɔɔ paahaɣ ɛyaa sakɩyɛ nʋmɔʋ, takayɩsɩ nzɩ sɩhaɣ ɛyaa nʋmɔʋ yɔ papɩzɩɣ pamʋ-sɩ fenaɣ kajalaɣ kɩyakʋ wiye ɛlɛ pɩwɛɛ se paɖaŋ fenasɩ naanza pʋcɔ nɛ palabɩnɩ-sɩ tʋmɩyɛ
text_en: Permits are limited to protect the canyon, and become available on the 1st day of the month, four months prior to the start month.

text: Ye mbʋ, takayaɣ ŋga kahaɣ ɛyʋ waɖɛ se esiɣ kizinziku paa kɩyakʋ ŋgʋ Agoza fenaɣ taa yɔ, papɩzɩɣ pamʋ-kɛ kpaɣnɩ Kɔlaɣ fenaɣ kajalaɣ kɩyakʋ wiye
text_en: Thus, a backcountry permit for any start date in May becomes available on 1 Jan.

text: Ɖoŋ ɖoŋ lɛ kɩyakʋ ŋgʋ pañɩtɩɣ paha nʋmɔʋ se ɛyaa ɩma pa-hɩla yɔ, ɛyaa sakɩyɛ pɔzʋʋ se powoki lona wena a-hɩla sɛwa ɛzɩ Bright Angel Campground kadaɣ ŋga kɔñɔtɩnɩ Phamtom Ranch yɔ, a-taa.
text_en: Space for the most popular areas, such as the Bright Angel Campground adjacent to Phantom Ranch, generally fill up by the requests received on first date they are opened to reservations.

text: Mba pahaɣ nʋmɔʋ se pɛyɛlɩ peeɖe patɩɖɔɔ nɛ mba pɛlɛyɩɣ kɔm yɔ mba pahaɣ nʋmɔʋ.
text_en: There are a limited number permits reserved for walk-in requests available on a first come, first served basis.

text: Nsaɣ lɔɖɩyɛ se ŋsu Africa hadɛ tɛtʋ naa taa, peyee ŋnaɣ peyee tɛtʋ kɔjɔka pɩsɔsɩna aleɣya nʋmɔʋ wobu nɩmaŋ.
text_en: Entering Southern Africa by car is an amazing way to see all the region's beauty as well as to get to places off the normal tourist routes.

text: Eyʋ pɩsɩɣ ɛkpaɣ lɔrɩyɛ yem ñɩɖɛ kɔsɩkɔsɩ 4̀X4 nɛ ɛla ɛtaɣmaɣ pɩlɩnaa hɔlɩŋ weyi ɛsɔlɩ ɛtaa wobu yɔ ɛsɩna mbʋ sɩɩ 4X4 lɔrɩyɛ kɛsɛɣ pɩtɩfɛyɩ hɔlɩŋ ɛnɩ ɛtaa.
text_en: This can be done in a normal car with careful planning but a 4x4 is highly advised and many locations are only accessible with a high wheel base 4x4.

text: Pɩtɩ pɔsɩ ɛyʋ ɛsɔɔ alɩwaatʋ ndʋ ɛɖɔŋ ɛtaɣmaɣ labʋ yɔ se paa Africa hadɛ tɛtʋ taa wezu caɣʋ wɛ hɛɛ yɔ, ɛɖɔkʋ ɛlakaɖɩ mpʋ pɩyɔɔƴɔ, tɛtʋ lɛŋdʋ taa wezu caɣʋ wɛ haɣʋ.
text_en: Keep in mind while planning that although Southern Africa is stable not all neighboring countries are.

text: Visa waa lidiyee nɛ tɩlasɩ naa wɛ ndi ndi pɩlɩnaa paa tɛtʋ ndu tɩkamasɩ tɛ paɣtʋ nɛ pɩlɩnaa ɖɔɖɔ tɛtʋ ndʋ tɩtaa ŋlɩnaa yɔ.
text_en: Visa requirements and costs vary from nation to nation and are affected by the country you come from.

text: Paa tɛtʋ ndʋ nɛ tɩtɛ paɣtʋ pɩlɩnaa kpɛdɛyɛ taa tɩlasɩ alɩwaatʋ ndʋ ɛyʋ wɛ lɔrɩyɛ taa yɔ.
text_en: Each country also has unique laws requiring what emergency items need to be in the car.

text: Victoria lɩm faɣlaɣ ke tɛtʋ ndʋ tɩwɛ Zimbabwe wɩsɩ ɖʋɖʋyɛ, kpaɣna Livingstone kaɣmaɣ, Zambie nɛ Botswana cɔlɔ.
text_en: Victoria Falls is a town in the western portion of Zimbabwe, across the border from Livingstone, Zambia, and near Botswana.

text: Tɛtʋ wɛ lɩm faɣlaɣ cɔlɔ, nɛ pɩtɛ kɔjɔka hɔŋ ɛyaa, ɛlɛ tɛtʋ tɩwɛ waɣzaɣ mba pɔsɔlɩ yɛlʋʋ se pɔcɔna ɖɔɖɔ avema sakɩyɛ yɔ.
text_en: The town lies immediately next to the falls, and they are the major attraction, but this popular tourist destination offers both adventure seekers and sightseers plenty of opportunities for a longer stay.

text: Tɛʋ tɛ alɩwaatʋ taa lɛ (saŋkayɩŋ-lakɩŋ), lɩm tɛ caɣcagyaɣ kpaɣ nɛ lɩm falʋʋ ɖɔɖɔ wɛ kaɖɛ.
text_en: In the rainy season (November to March), the water volume will be higher and the Falls will be more dramatic.

text: Eyʋ ɛɖɔŋ hɔlʋ ŋgʋ, ɛwondu sɩkɩ-lɩm nɛ yee ɛɖɛsɩ koŋdɔlɩko yaa ɛɖɔŋ lɩm faɣlaɣ hɔɔlʋ taa yɔ, lɩm mɩsɩɣ ɛyaɣ.
text_en: You are guaranteed to get wet if you cross the bridge or walk along the trails winding near the Falls.

text: Ɖɔɖɔ lɛ, ɛsɩna mbu lɩm tɛ caɣcaɣyaɣ kpaɣ yɔ, pʋnɛ pɩyekinaa se ɛyʋ ɛwɛ ɛcɔnaa lɩm faɣlaɣ yɔ, ɛpɩsɩ ɛna polɩŋ; pɩlakɩ ɛsɛ yɔ fɩɖɩɩ.
text_en: On the other hand, it is precisely because the volume of water is so high that your viewing of the actual Falls will be obscured—by all the water!

text: Tutankhamun pɩlaɣʋ (KV62). KV62 pɩsɩ pɩkenaa pɩlaɣʋ ŋgʋ kɩ-tɔm kɩlɩ tɔyʋʋ yɔ fɛnʋʋ taa peye, ɛsɩna pɩnaɣ 1922, Carter na wiyaʋ evebu tɛ pɩlaɣʋ pɩwɛ ɛsɩ nabʋyʋ tɩtokɩnɩ-kʋ.
text_en: Tomb of Tutankhamun (KV62). KV62 may be the most famous of the tombs in the Valley, the scene of Howard Carter's 1922 discovery of the almost intact royal burial of the young king.

text: Paɣmaɣsɩ-kʋ nɛ awiyaa lɛla pɩlaŋ yɔ, Tutankhamum tɛ pɩlaɣʋ wɛ cɔnaʋ pɩkɩlɩ lɛlɩŋ mbu pʋyɔɔyɔ, kɩwɛ n̂ɩɩ nɛ ɖɔɖɔ lɛ, patɩkɩlɩ ajanaa labʋ kɩyaɣ.
text_en: Compared to most of the other royal tombs, however, the tomb of Tutankhamun is barely worth visiting, being much smaller and with limited decoration.

text: Yee nɔyʋ ɛsɔlaa se ɛna ebe laba sɩŋ aliwaatʋ ndʋ palɩsaɣ wiyaʋ pilimiye se pɛlɛsɩ ɖɛ yɔ, pɩɖɩsɩ-ɩ, mbʋ pʋyɔɔ yɔ, ñʋʋ nɛ laɣsɩ kpoyɩŋ ɖeke ɛ-pɩsɩ ɛna.
text_en: Anyone interested in seeing evidence of the damage to the mummy done during attempts to remove it from the coffin will be disappointed as only the head and shoulders are visible.

text: Kɔjɔka wondu tatasɩ wɛʋ pɩlaɣʋ taa, powona-tʋ Cairo, Egypte wondu pɩluu taa.
text_en: The fabulous riches of the tomb are no longer in it, but have been removed to the Egyptian Museum in Cairo.

text: Akɔmaa mba pɛfɛyɩ-nɩ aliwaatʋ, pɩwɛ kɛsɛ pɩkɩlɩ yee powoba ɖe-lɛŋdɛ se pekilimi pɛsɛ yɔɔ.
text_en: Visitors with limited time would be best to spend their time elsewhere.

text: Phnom Krom wɛ kiloomɛta waa 12 nɛ Siem Reap tɛ hadɛ-wɩsɩ ɖʋɖʋyɛ. Paama kpaaŋ kʋnaa pɩyaɣ yaɣ pɩcɔ nɛ pɩnaɣ 900 lɩɩ. Alɩwaatʋ nɖʋ tʋtʋzina Yasovarman tɛ kewiitʋ alɩwaatʋ.
text_en: Phnom Krom, 12 km southwest of Siem Reap. This hilltop temple was built at the end of the 9th century, during the reign of King Yasovarman.

text: Kpaŋ tɛ alɩwaatʋ fɩɖɩɩ wɛtʋ nɛ Tonle Sap tɛ lɩm mbʊ pɩkpeŋ yɔ, pɩwɛ camɩyɛ se ɛyʋ ɛpka pɩyaɣ ñʋtaa nɛ ɛcɔna.
text_en: The gloomy atmosphere of the temple and the view over the Tonle Sap lake make the climb to the hill worthwhile.

text: Pɩwɛ camɩyɛ se ɛyʋ ɛwolo nɛ ɛcɔna tɛtʋ tɩna nɛ ɛcaɣ kpɩyʋ sɛ ɛ-cɔna tɛtʋ yɔ, pɩwɛ kɔjɔka.
text_en: A visit to the site can be conveniently combined with a boat trip to the lake.

text: Pɩcɔ nɛ ɛyʋ pɩsɩ na ɛsʋ kpaaŋ taa, pɩpɔsʋ ɛwɛna Angkor Pass maɣyaɣ nɛ ɛtaasɔ ɖɔɖɔ ɛtɛ passport yɔ yee ɛsʋ Tonle Sap taa.
text_en: The Angkor Pass is needed to enter the temple so do not forget to bring your passport along when heading to Tonle Sap.

text: Jerusalem keena Israel tɛtʋ ndʊ tɩtɩkɩlɩ walʋʋ tɛtʋ tɩnɛ taa, paa ajɛyɛ lɛna nɛ Organisation des Nations Unies ɛtɩzɩ se Israel lɛ tɛtʋ sʋsɔtʋ
text_en: Jerusalem is the capital and largest city of Israel, though most other countries and the United Nations do not recognize it as Israel's capital.

text: Tɛtʋ kɩbɩŋdʋ tɩwɛ Judee piyasɩ yaɣ sɩwɛ cɔjɔka pɩnsɩ egbaŋ egbaŋ.
text_en: The ancient city in the Judean Hills has a fascinating history spanning thousands of years.

text: Tɛtʋ wɛ cɩɖɩ cɩɖɩ pɩha ɛsɔnaa mba panadozo: Juda sɔŋsɩ, Kristʋ sɔŋsɩ nɛ malɩŋ sɔnsɩ nɛ kalɩzaɣ taa caɣʋ, nɛ samtʋ, nɛ aƴɛnɛ tɛtʋ
text_en: The city is holy to the three monotheistic religions - Judaism, Christianity and Islam, and serves as a spiritual, religious, and cultural center.

text: Esɩna mbʋ pike ɛsɔ sɛtʋ tɛtʋ nɛ tɛtʋ kɩbɩŋtʋ lɛ,  Jerusalem wɛ aleɣya nʋmɔʋ wobu tɛtʋ sʋsɔtʋ sʋsɔtʋ taa
text_en: Due to the religious significance of the city, and in particular the many sites of the Old City area, Jerusalem is one of the main tourist destinations in Israel.

text: Jerusalem wɛna caanaʋ taa wondu nɛ tɛtʋ naa ndi ndi nɛ wondu ɖɩyaɖɛ nɛ tɔnaɣ ɖɩtɔɔ lona wona a-wɛ kpekpeka nɛ ɛyaa ɖɔʋ a-taa ɖɩɖɔ yɔ.
text_en: Jerusalem has many historic, archeological and cultural sites, along with vibrant and crowded shopping centers, cafés, and restaurants.

text: Equateur paɣtʋ pɔsʋ se pʋcɔ nɛ Cuba-tʋ sʋʋ pɛt-tɛtʋ taa lɛ, pɩpɔsʋ se ɛwɛnɩ taɣkaɣyaɣ ŋga kaɣ-haɣyɩ waɖɛ nɛ pʋcɔ ɛsʋ ɛsɔdaa lɔrɩyɛ nɛ etii peyee ya ɛtɩŋnɩ tɛtʋ kaɣmaɣ.
text_en: Ecuador requires that Cuban citizens receive an invitation letter prior to entering Ecuador through international airports or frontier admission points.

text: Equateur tɛ mɩnɩstrɩ weyi ɛcɔŋna Equateur nɛ ajɛɛ lɛɛna patabalɩyɛ yɔ, ɛ-ñɩɩ nimbiyee kataa pʋcɔ, nɛ ɛkom ɖɔɖɔ ɖɔ paɣtʋ naa lɛndʋ.
text_en: This letter must be legalized by the Ecuadorian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and comply with certain requirements.

text: Paɖʋ paɣtʋ ŋdu se pɩpɩsɩ pɩsɩnaa ajɛɛyɛ ana a-nalɛɛ a-tɛ ɛyaa tɛ wobu nɛ kɔm.
text_en: These requirements are designed to provide an organized migratory flow between both countries.

text: Cuba ñɩma mba pɛ-wɛnɩ America taɣkaɣyaɣ ŋga kaɣhaɣ wɛ waɖɛ se pasʋʋ America ɛjaɖɛ taa yɔ, powokɩ Equateur ɛ-jaɖɛ lonee taa caɣyʋ tʋmɩyɛ taa nɛ pɛ cɛlɩ-wɛ taɣkaɣyaɣ ŋga kaɣhaɣ wɛ wadɛ se papatasɩ wɛʋ cɛyɩtʋ natʋyʋ taa pɩlɩ-nɛ takayɩsɩ tɔm taa.
text_en: Cuban citizens who are US green card holders should visit an Ecuadorian Consulate to obtain an exemption to this requirement.

text: Pʋpɔzuu se paa wɛyɩ ɛ-tɛ passport ɛ-tala fenasɩ lodo nɛ pɩcɔ kɩsɩ yee ɛ-caɣ ɛ-sʋ tɛtʋ taa. Pʋpɔsʋ ɖɔɖɔ se tikee ŋgʋ paa weyɩ ɛ-yakɩ yɔ, kɩwɩlɩ fenasɩ ɛsɩnaa ewoki labʋ tɛtʋ taa yɔ.
text_en: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months beyond your travel dates. A round/onward trip ticket is needed to prove the length of your stay.

text: Cɔʋ nɛ cɔnaɣʋ wɛ kɛsɛ yee ɛyaa ɛ-ɖɔwaa, yee ŋwɛ ñeɖeke yaa ɛwɛ naalɛ yɔ, ɛñɩnɩ nabɛyɛ ɛ-sɔsɩ mɩyɔɔ ɛ-tala nanza ya loɖo nɛ pɩtaakɩlɩ mɛ lidiyee mʋʋ.
text_en: Tours are cheaper for larger groups, so if you're by yourself or with just one friend, try to meet other people and form a group of four to six for a better per-person rate.

text: Paa mbʊ yɔ, pɩʈɩ pɔsɩ se ɛyʋ eɖoo tɔm ŋdʋ tɩyɔɔ, mbʊ pʋyɔɔ yɔ, aleɣya nʋmɔʋ woɖaa naɣ se pʋpɔsʋ se paɖʋ saŋsɩ pɔ-lɔrɛ taa.
text_en: However, this shouldn't really be off your concern, because often tourists are shuffled around to fill the cars.

text: Pɩwɛsɩ pɩcɛʈɩɣ ɛyaa nɛ pɔcɔna se pɩwɛ se pɛhɛyɩ lidiyee sakɩyɛ.
text_en: It seems actually to be more a way of tricking people into believing they have to pay more.

text: Machu Picchu tɛtʋ nɛ hayi yɔɔ lɛ, pʋʋ sʋsɔʋ wɛ, nɛ ɛyaa pasɩ pɔsɔlɩ kɛlɛm kɛlɛm waa kpaʋ nɛ tɛtʋ yɔkaa nɛ mbu pɩkasɩ yɔ pɩtɩfɛyɩ
text_en: Towering above the north end of Machu Picchu is this steep mountain, often the backdrop to many photos of the ruins.

text: Ye ŋgbaɣ nɩ pdɛɛ yɔ, pouwɛ sondɔ pasɩ ptɛ lɛ, kaɣgbaɣ wɛnɩ cɛyɩtʋ pɩŋ, ɛlɛ ɛya mba pɛwɛ kaalɛtɔ nɛ tɔnʋʋ taa kpekpeka yɔ, 45 minutes talɩɣ wɛ.
text_en: It looks a bit daunting from below, and it is a steep and difficult ascent, but most reasonably fit persons should be able to make it in about 45 minutes.

text: Poɖonɩ pɛ teŋdema ɖʋ nɩ nomoʋ, pɩsaɣ nɩ kɛjɛlŋzɩ daa lɛ, paɖu ñɩɩtʋ nɩmasɩ sé sɩtelɩ eya
text_en: Stone steps are laid along most of the path, and in the steeper sections steel cables provide a supporting handrail.

text: Pdobou se, pgaɣ mɩ nɩʋ pdɩfɛɩ, pyolɛ ɛɖɔki mɩnaŋ taa nɩ pɩcɛyɩ kɔzɔ kɔzɔ yolɩm dɛ awɛ daa, mbu yɔ, pbɩzɣ ni prɛ rom kɛlɛwu yem
text_en: That said, expect to be out of breath, and take care in the steeper portions, especially when wet, as it can become dangerous quickly.

text: Klɔmʋ nakʋyʋ ñɔtini ñʋ taa, pbɔzʋ si pcɛzi kʋ, kidʋkʋyi ɛlɛ kidiwali
text_en: There's a tiny cave near the top that must be passed through, it is quite low and a rather tight squeeze.

text: Teŋgu yɔɔ lɔɖiɛ daa mpiziɣ ni ŋna Galapagos ajɛya ni añitʋ, ɛsi Charles Darwin ilabu 1835 pinaɣ daa yɔ
text_en: Seeing the sites and wildlife of the Galapagos is best done by boat, just as Charles Darwin did it in 1835.

text: Teŋgu yɔ loɖa wena adɛziɣ Galapagos ɛjaɖɛ yo adaliɣ 60 ni paa pinɖɛ lɛ, digbaɣ ɛya si 8 ni ŋwolo ŋsini 100
text_en: Over 60 cruise ships ply the Galapagos waters - ranging in size from 8 to 100 passengers.

text: Ɛya sakiyɛ paziɣ polona fayii picɔ kiyakʋ tali ( mbʋ yo, teŋgu yɔ lora suu paa tam wɛɛ sɔsɔna taa)
text_en: Most people book their place well in advance (as the boats are usually full during the high season).

text: Pbɔsʋ se ŋtili ŋzii se tʋmilaɖʋ weyi ɛjɔlɔ mbaziɣ loniye yɔ, pbɔzina se ɛkɛna Galapagos dʋ weyɩ ɛsɩm ɛdʋmɩyɛ kalɛɛtʋ yɔ nɩ pɩdɛ ɛyʋ ɛnʋ, ɛtlɩ teŋgu yɔ lɔɖaa ndɩ ndɩ
text_en: Be sure the agent through whom you book is a Galapagos specialist with a good knowledge of a wide variety of ships.

text: Mbɔ pwɩlɩɣnɩ kalaa se mɩdɛ cɛyɩtʋ yaa mɩtɛ kɛzaɣ lɩɣnɩ teŋgu yo lora wena sɩ akɛnɩ kbana pɛssɩnda yɔ
text_en: This will ensure that your particular interests and/or constraints are matched with the ship most suitable to them.

text: Pɩcɔ nɩ Españɩa mba talɩ 16th century lɛ, Inca mba ɛkpa Chilli ɛjaɖɛ nɩ ɖɩhayou mba yomɩye ɛlɛ tɛtʋ ñɩma Araucania mba ( Mapuche) ɖɛwa paɣcaɣ Chilliɛjarɛ hɛkɛʋ nɩ kɩdɛ hadɛ.
text_en: Before the Spanish arrived in the 16th century, northern Chile was under Inca rule while the indigenous Araucanians (Mapuche) inhabited central and southern Chile.

text: Mapuche mba kɛkɛ ɖɔɖɔ America dɛ kɛdɛzaɣ tɛtʋ ñɩma mba paawɛ padi yɔɔ yɔ, chilli hiɣ kidi yɔɔ wɛʋ lɛ, pabɩsɩ Españia ŋzulumiɛ ɓɛŋɖɛ.
text_en: The Mapuche were also one of the last independent American indigenous groups, that were not fully absorbed into Spanish-speaking rule until after Chile's independence.

text: Paa Chilli ɛjaɖɛ ɛhiɣ ɖɩdɩ yɔɔ weʋ 1810 pinaɣ taa yɔ ( Napoleon dɛ yoŋ ŋdi ŋdi weyɩ eyebi Españɩa ɛjaɖɛ komna lone kpɛɖɛ pɩŋzɩ caɓɩ), ɛlɛ 1818 pnaɣ daa pawabɩ Españia piŋ
text_en: Although Chile declared independence in 1810 (amid the Napoleonic wars that left Spain without a functioning central government for a couple of years), decisive victory over the Spanish was not achieved until 1818.

text: Repubiliki Dominiki (Spanish: República Dominicana) kɛ Karayib mba ɛjaɖɛ nɖɩ ɖɩkpaɣ wɩsɩ ɖɩlɩyɛ taa lɩm hɛkʋ taa tɛtʋ ndʋ payaɣ se Hisipaniyola yɔ tɩ-hɔɔlʋʋ nɛ Hayiti ñakpaɣ hɔɔlʋʋ lɛɛkʋ.
text_en: The Dominican Republic (Spanish: República Dominicana) is a Caribbean country that occupies the eastern half of the island of Hispaniola, which it shares with Haiti

text: Pɩtasɩnɩ pʋŋ nɛ teŋgu nɔɔ kañɩŋa ŋga kahʋlʋmɩ camɩyɛ yɔ lɛ, ɛjaɖɛ nɖɩ ɖɩ-taa Erɔɔpɩ mba kajalaɣ tɛtʋ sɔsɔtʋ kɩbɩndʋ wɛɛ, nɛ lɛɛlɛɛyɔ tɩwɛ Santo Domingo taa.
text_en: Besides white sand beaches and mountain landscapes, the country is home to the oldest European city in the Americas, now part of Santo Domingo.

text: Taino mba nɛ Karayib mba kaacalɩnɩ wɛʋ lɩm hɛkʋ taa tɛtʋ ndʋ tɩ-yɔɔ. Karayib mba yɔɔdʋʋ Arawakaŋ kʋnʋŋ nɛ patalɩ peeɖe pɩnaɣ 10 000 pʋcɔ nɛ palʋlʋʋ Yesu.
text_en: The island was first inhabited by the Taínos and Caribes. The Caribes were an Arawakan-speaking people who had arrived around 10,000 BCE.

text: Ajɛɛ kɩfana ñɩnɩyaa mba palɩnɩ Erɔɔpɩ yɔ patalaa nɛ pɩla pɩnzɩ pazɩ lɛ, Ɛsɩpaañɩ ñɩma mba pɔkɔma se pamʋ ɛjaɖɛ yɔ palaba nɛ Taino mba ñʋʋ pasɩ pɩdɩɩfɛyɩ
text_en: Within a few short years following the arrival of European explorers, the population of Tainos had significantly been reduced by the Spanish conquerors

text: Fray Bartolomé de las Casas (Tratado de las Indias) kaayɔɔdaa se Ɛsɩpaañɩ ñɩma mba pɔkɔma se pamʋ ɛjaɖɛ yɔ paakʋ Tainos mba ɛzɩ 100 000 mbʋ yɔ kpaɣnɩ pɩnaɣ 1492 nɛ piwolo pɩnaɣ 1498.
text_en: Based on Fray Bartolomé de las Casas (Tratado de las Indias) between 1492 and 1498 the Spanish conquerors killed around 100,000 Taínos.

text: Jardín de la Unión. Paama lone ŋɖɩ se ɖɩkɛnɩ 17th-century dɛ pʋlʋ nakʋyʋ saɣmaɣ ɖgbeliye, loniye ŋɖɩ ɖda mam lɛ Templo de San Diego yeke koŋ pikaza.
text_en: Jardín de la Unión. This space was built as the atrium for a 17th-century convent, of which the Templo de San Diego is the sole surviving building.

text: Peye pɩssa nɩ piwɛ ɛzi loniye sɔssɔɖɛ daa yɔ ni wɩssɩ nɩ ɖoo tam lɛ nabʋyʋ ɖɔŋnɩ ɖɔm beɖe
text_en: It now functions as the central plaza, and always has a lot of things going on, day and night.

text: Tɔnaɣsɩ pɛdɩya nabɛyɛɛ wɛ kaɣdaɣ taa peyee pɩkazɩ nɩ danaɣ nɩ pwokɩ wssɩ ɖʋ lɛ, yondu teya lakɩ aleya hɛkʋda gazebo taa.
text_en: There are a number of restaurants surrounding the garden, and in the afternoons and evening there free concerts are often given from the central gazebo.

text: Callejon del Beso (Alley of the kiss). Sɔlɩm ɛsso zɛyɛ naɖɩɛ wɛ ɖeŋɖe teŋdema naalɛ possi ɖama ni hɛyaɣ ɛsi paakɛdini 69 centimeters yo.
text_en: Callejon del Beso (Alley of the Kiss). Two balconies separated by only 69 centimeters is home of an old love legend.

text: Ŋñita ni ŋhɩɣ pɩya lidiye pɔyɔssɩ nassɩyɛ pasɩ yɔ, sɩgɛdiɣŋ tɔm ŋdʋ.
text_en: For a few pennies some children will tell you the story.

text: Bowen Island gɛnɩ kɩyaku kʋyʋmʋ kɔzɔɖɔ tɛm dɛ yɛlʋ, nɩ yɛlʋ mɓʋ pdaa lɛ ansayi kpɩyɩŋ sau wɛ, ɖama katʋʋ, faɖɛ na daa woɓu, tɔkɩyɛ, nɛ pdassɩ pɩyɔɔ.
text_en: Bowen Island is a popular day trip or weekend excursion offering kayaking, hiking, shops, restaurants, and more.

text: Ɛya mba pɛwɛ Hwe Sound gɛ Vancouver cɔlɔ, nɩ pzɖe wobu wɛ kɛlʋ yem plɩna lɩm yɔɔ loɖa tɛ tɔmɩyɛ labu yɔɔ kaɣkaɣmaɣ Granville Island kɛɛ Vancouver tɛtʋ hɛkʋda.
text_en: This authentic community is located in Howe Sound just off Vancouver, and is easily accessed via scheduled water taxis departing Granville Island in downtown Vancouver.

text: Mbaa nɩ pɔzɔlɩ awayɩ ameya tɔm yɔ, teŋgu ni essoda paklɔmʋ wɛ feveɖe.
text_en: For those who enjoy outdoor activities, a trek up the Sea to Sky corridor is essential.

text: Wondu wɛ liidiye Wisitɩlɛɛrɩ (ŋkʋyɩnɩ Vankuvɛɛrɩ ŋɖɔŋ ñɩɣyʋʋ kʋɖʋm nɛ hɔɔlʋʋ pʋcɔ ŋtalɩ peeɖe), ɛlɛ ɛyaa sakɩyɛ sɩm tɛtʋ ndʋ pɩlɩɩna ajɛya kɩgbɛndʋʋ aleɣya wena paalabɩ peeɖe pɩnaɣ 2010 taa yɔ.
text_en: Whistler (1.5 hour drive from Vancouver) is expensive but well-known because of the 2010 Winter Olympics.

text: Nikaɣ alɩwaatʋ taa lɛ, ɩfanɩ sikii aleɣya wena palakɩ Amerika nɛ hayi kiŋ yɔ a-taa wena akpaɖaa yɔ, nɛ soŋaɣ alɩwaatʋ taa lɛ ɩmaɣzɩ pʋʋ taa cɛɛcɛ saʋ nɛ ɩna.
text_en: In the winter, enjoy some of the best skiing in North America, and in the summer try some authentic mountain biking.

text: Pɩwɛɛ se ŋwolo nɛ paha-ŋ waɖɛ lɔŋ pʋcɔ. Pɩwɛɛ se paha-ŋ waɖɛ pʋcɔ nɛ ŋhɩnɩ Sirena tɛtʋ taa.
text_en: Permits must be reserved in advance. You must have a permit to stay overnight at Sirena.

text: Sirena ɖeke kɛnɩ laŋ yɔɔ kandɩyʋʋ tʋmɩyɛ nɖɩ ɖɩhaɣ ɖɩzʋyɛ nɛ tɔɔnasɩ nzɩ sɩwɛ miŋ yɔ, pɩtasɩna kizinzikiŋ lɛ. Lewoona, Saŋ Pedriyoo nɛ Losi Patoosi, kizinzikiŋ ɖeke pahaɣ, tɔɔnaɣ fɛyɩ.
text_en: Sirena is the only ranger station that offers dormitory lodging and hot meals in addition to camping. La Leona, San Pedrillo, and Los Patos offer only camping with no food service.

text: Laŋ yɔɔ kandɩyʋʋ tʋmɩyɛ nɖɩ ɖɩwɛ Puyertoo Jiimenɛɛzɩ yɔ, ɖɩpɩzɩɣ ɖɩha waɖɛ kaɖaɣ yɔɔ, ɛlɛ paatisiɣ takayɩsɩ nzɩ pamʋʋna liidiye menziiniwaa taa yɔ.
text_en: It is possible to secure park permits directly from the Ranger Station in Puerto Jiménez, but they do not accept credit cards

text: Kaɖɩsɩ tʋmɩyɛ (nɖɩ payaɣ se MINAE yɔ), pʋcɔ nɛ alɩwaatʋ ndʋ paɖʋwa yɔ tɩtalɩ lɛ, ɖɩɩhaɣ kaɖaɣ yɔɔ waɖɛ takayaɣ nɛ pɩcɛzɩ fenaɣ kʋɖʋmaɣ.
text_en: The Park Service (MINAE) does not issue park permits more than one month in advance of anticipated arrival.

text: Tʋmɩyɛ nɖɩ payaɣ se KɔfɩNɛɛtɩ Ɛl Sɔɔlɩ yɔ, ye ɛyʋ ɛsɔɔlaa se ɛñɩɣ kaaʋ evemiye kʋɖʋmɖɩyɛ tɛ wɛsʋʋ takayaɣ yɔɔ kɔyɔ, ɖɩmʋʋ-ɩ liidiye Dɔɔlaarɩwaa 30 yaa 10. Ye ŋsɔɔlaa se ŋnɩɩ pɩ-taa nɛ pɩkɩlɩ yɔ, wolo pɛ-tɛ ɛntɛrɩnɛtɩɩ lone Korikoovado yɔɔ.
text_en: CafeNet El Sol offers a reservation service for a fee of US$30, or $10 for one-day passes; details on their Corcovado page.

text: Kuuki lɩm hɛkʋ taa tɛtʋ kɛ ɛjaɖɛ nɖɩ ɖɩtam nɔɔ faaa nɛ Nuvɛɛlɩ-zelandɩ yɔ, nɛ tɩwɛ Polineezii, Pasiifiki nɛ hadɛ kiŋ teŋgu sɔsɔʋ hɛkʋ taa.
text_en: The Cook Islands are an island country in free association with New Zealand, located in Polynesia, in the middle of the South Pacific Ocean.

text: Pɩkɛ lɩm hɛkʋ taa tɛtʋ kɩgbɛndʋʋ mbʋ pɩ-taa wɛ lɩm hɛkʋ taa tɛtʋ ɛzɩ 15 mbʋ yɔ, mbʋ papɩzɩɣ patayɩ-pʋ teŋgu sɔsɔʋ walanzɩ mbʋ pɩtalɩɣ kilomɛtawaa miilliyɔɔwaa 2.2 mbʋ yɔ tam nabʋlɛ.
text_en: It is an archipelago with 15 islands spread out over 2.2 million km2 of ocean.

text: Ɛzɩma lɩm hɛkʋ taa tɛtʋ nɛ Hawayii pɛwɛnɩ alɩwaatʋ kɩgbɛndʋʋ kʋɖʋmʋm yɔ, ɛyaa kpakɩɣ-tʋ ɛzɩ "Hawayii nɛ pɩ-tɛɛ kiŋ tɛtʋ" yɔ.
text_en: With the same time zone as Hawaii, the islands are sometimes thought of as "Hawaii down under".

text: Paa kɩwɛ ŋñɩɩ nɛ pɩkɩlɩ yɔ, kɩtɔzʋʋ-ɖʋ ɛzʋtʋyaa mba pekilimi Hawayii yɔɔ yɔ, pʋcɔ nɛ pamaɣ ɛjaɖɛ nɖɩ, ɛsɩyɛgbena agɔma ɖɩsɩ nɛ ɛsɩndaa wobu lɛɛbʋ taatɩɩwɛda lɛ.
text_en: Though smaller, it reminds some elderly visitors of Hawaii before statehood without all the large tourist hotels and other development.

text: Kuuki lɩm hɛkʋ taa tɛtʋ fɛyɩna tɛtʋ sɔsɔtʋ, ɛlɛ lɩm hɛkʋ taa tɛtʋ ndɩ ndɩ 15 wɛna tɩ-taa. Pɩ-taa ndʋ tɩkpaɖaa yɔ lɛ Raarotɔŋga nɛ Ayiitutaakii.
text_en: The Cook Islands do not have any cities but are composed of 15 different islands. The main ones are Rarotonga and Aitutaki.

text: Sɔnɔ, ñɩm ajɛya taa, agɔma ɖɩsɩ taa kuduyiŋ weyi ɩkpaɖɩ ɖeu yɔ, ɩ-pɛdʋʋ pɩsɩ ajana pʋyʋ.
text_en: In developed countries today, providing deluxe bed and breakfasts has been raised to a sort of art-form.

text: Yee mbʋ agbaa wena akɛ B&B waa yɔ, alʋkɩnɩ ɖama kɔzɩ kɔzɩ hɔɔlɩŋ naalɛ taa : kuduyuu yɔɔ nɛ sɔntɔ yɔɔ.
text_en: At the top end, B&Bs obviously compete mainly on two main things: bedding and breakfast.

text: Pʋyɔɔ lɛ, agbaa wena akɩlɩ weewee hɔɔlʋʋ ŋgʋ kɩ-taa yɔ a-taa, ŋpɩzɩɣ nɛ ŋna hɛzɩyɛ kaɖʋnaa mba pakaɖaa yɔ, pɩtɩla sumɖe nɖɩ palabɩna nesi yɔ yaa kaɖʋ kɩbɩnʋʋ nakʋyʋ.
text_en: Accordingly, at the finest such establishments one is apt to find the most luxurious bedding, maybe a handmade quilt or an antique bed.

text: Sɔntɔ taa, papɩzɩɣ paɖʋ hɔɔlʋʋ ŋgʋ kɩ-taa anaam tɔɔnasɩ, yaa tɔɔnasɩ nzɩ pakɩlɩɣ pɛdʋʋ agɔma ɖɩɣa ŋga ka-taa yɔ.
text_en: Breakfast may include seasonal delights of the region or the host's speciality dish.

text: Hɔɔlʋʋ ŋgʋ palakɩna tʋmɩyɛ yɔ, kɩpɩzɩɣ kɩkɛ caanaʋ taa kuduyuu kɩbɩnʋʋ nakʋyʋ, ŋgʋ kɩ-taa wɛ wondu kɩbɩndʋ ndɩ ndɩ yɔ, kajasɩ nzɩ pɔñɔɔzɩ-sɩ camɩyɛ yɔ, nɛ lɩm yaʋ pɔʋ.
text_en: The setting might be an historic old building with antique furnishings, manicured grounds and a swimming pool.

text: Se ɛyʋ ɛkpa ɛ-maɣmaɣ ɛ-lɔɔɖɩyɛ taa nɛ ewolo nʋmɔʋ ɖooo poliŋ taa lɔɔɖɩyɛ nɖɩ ɖɩ-taa, pɩkɛ mbʋ pɩwɛ kɛlɛʋ nɛ ɛyaa sɔɔlɩ pɩ-labʋ yɔ.
text_en: Getting into your own car and heading off on a long road trip has an intrinsic appeal in its simplicity.

text: Ɛzɩ pɩwɛʋ ndɩ nɛ lɔɔɖa sɔsɔna yɔ, pɩtʋʋ fɛyɩ se ñɔ-lɔɔɖɩyɛ saʋ tɛmɩ-ŋ malɩnaʋ, nɩ ŋsɩm ɖi-ɖoŋ kamaɣ.
text_en: Unlike larger vehicles, you are probably already familiar with driving your car and know its limitations.

text: Kizinziku siɣu ɛyʋ lɛlʋ tɛtʋ yɔɔ yaa tɛtʋ sɔsɔtʋ natʋyʋ taa, paa tɩpaɣlɩ ɛzɩma yɔ, pɩpɩzɩɣ nɛ pɩhɔ kɩdɛkɛdaa nabɛyɛ lɩmaɣza kɛlɛʋ yem.
text_en: Setting up a tent on private property or in a town of any size can easily attract unwanted attention.

text: Tobi lɛ, ña-maɣmaɣ ñɔ-lɔɔɖɩyɛ saʋ kɛnɩ nʋmɔʋ kɩbaŋgʋ ŋgʋ kɩ-yɔɔ nɛ ŋwolo nɔmɔʋ habɩyɛ yɔɔ, ɛlɛ pɩɩpɩzɩɣ pɩsɩnɩ-ŋ nɛ "ŋsiɣ kizinzikiŋ".
text_en: In short, using your car is a great way to take a road trip but seldom in itself a way to "camp".

text: Ŋpɩzɩɣ nɛ ŋla kizinziku ñɔ-lɔɔɖɩyɛ taa yee ŋwɛnɩ lɔɔɖɩyɛ nɖɩ ɖɩwɛnɩ nɔnɔsɩ nɛ pohuuzi ɖɩ-ñʋʋ taa yɔ, nɖɩ ɖɩkʋyaa yɔ, lɔɔɖɩyɛ kɩɖaɣlɩyɛ yaa lɔɔɖɩyɛ nɖɩ papɩzɩɣ nɛ pekpiyi ɖi-kpelasi yɔ.
text_en: Car camping is possible if you have a large minivan, SUV, Sedan or Station Wagon with seats that lay down.

text: Agɔma ɖɩsɩ nasɩyɩ wɛnɩ ñɩm mbʋ sulukiŋ habɛɛ wena alakɩ tʋmɩyɛ nɛ hohou yɔ nɛ mɛlɛnaa mba pasɩɣlɩɣ ɛyaa yɔ peyeba ñɩɣlɩm pɩnzɩ taa yɔ, pʋcɔ nɛ palakɩ Caama you naalɛ ñɩŋgʋ, pɩnzɩ 19 taa yaa pɩnzɩ 20 ɖɩbaɣzɩyɛ.
text_en: Some hotels have a heritage from the golden age of steam railways and ocean liners; before the Second World War, in the 19th or early 20th centuries.

text: agɔma ɖɩsɩ nzɩ sɩ-taa alɩwaatʋ ndʋ tɩ-taa ñɩmdɩnaa nɛ caa akele waa sʋwaɣ. Nabʋyʋ taa pɩlakaɣ tɔɔnasɩ nzɩ pacatɩ camɩyɛ yɔ nɛ ɛyaa cakaɣ ɖoho taa wezuu peeɖe.
text_en: These hotels were where the rich and the famous of the day would stay, and often had fine dining and nightlife.

text: Pɛ-wɛtʋ taa natʋyʋ lɛ se pɔñɔɔzʋʋ wondu caanaʋ ñɔɔzʋʋ, pɛfɛyɩna kɛdɛzaɣ wondu ndʋ tɩlɩwa yɔ, nɛ po-kuduyiŋ kpadɩyɩ pazɩ.
text_en: The old fashioned fittings, the lack of the latest amenities, and a certain graceful agedness are also part of their character.

text: Paa ɖoŋ ɖoŋ lɛ pɛwɛ pa-tɩ yɔɔ kɔyɔ, nabʋyʋ taa pamʋʋ ɛgɔndʋ ajɛya ñʋndɩnaa nɛ awiya lɛɛna.
text_en: While they are usually privately owned, they sometimes accommodate visiting heads of state and other dignitaries.

text: Nɔmɔʋ woɖu weyi ɛwɛnɩ liidiye sakɩyɛ yɔ, ɛpɩzɩɣ nɛ ɛla ɖʋtʋ se ɛsʋʋ ɛsɔdaa lɔɔɖɩyɛ nɛ ɛcɔɔ ɛjaɖɛ, nɛ ɛɖaŋnɩ sɩŋʋʋ agɔma ɖɩsɩ nzɩ sɩ-taa alɩwaatʋ pazɩ pazɩ.
text_en: A traveller with piles of money might consider a round the world flight, broken up with stays in many of these hotels.

text: Nɔɔ tam ɛgɔndʋ mʋʋ nɔmɔʋ taa kɛnɩ ɛgbɛyɛ nɖɩ ɖɩtaŋ nɔmɔʋ woɖaa nɛ samaɣ ŋga kɛwɛ tɛtʋ sɔsɔtʋ ndʋ tɩ-taa powoki yɔ pɛ-hɛkʋ taa.
text_en: A hospitality exchange network is the organization that connects travelers with locals in the cities they are going to visit.

text: Pɩsa nɛ ɛyʋ sʋʋ ɛgbɛyɛ nɖɩ ɖɩ-taa lɛ, ɖoŋ ɖoŋ lɛ pɩwɛna-ɩ kɛlɛʋ yem se ecosi ɛntɛrnɛtɩ yɔɔ takayaɣ nakɛyɛ taa tɔm yɔɔ ; ɛlɛ agbaa naayɛ ñikiɣ pʋyɔɔ se patasɩ tɔm taa tazʋʋ.
text_en: Joining such a network usually just requires filling out an online form; although some networks offer or require additional verification.

text: Mba papɩzɩɣ nɛ pamʋ agɔma, pamaɣ pa-hɩla nɛ pʋwayɩ lɛ, palɩzɩ-yɛ menziini taa yaa paɖʋ-yɛ ɛntɛrɩnɛtɩɩ yɔɔ, nabʋyʋ taa pɔsɔzʋʋ nɔmɔʋ wobiyaa lalaa masɩ yaa tɔm ndʋ pɔcɔɔlʋʋ yɔ.
text_en: A listing of available hosts is then provided either in print and/or online, sometimes with references and reviews by other travelers.

text: Patʋlɩ couchsurfing nɔnɔsɩ kɔlaɣ fenaɣ 2004 taa, Ordinatɛɛrɩwaa ɖʋtʋ laɖʋ weyi payaɣ se Casey Fenton yɔ ehiɣ ɛsɔdaa lɔɔɖɩyɛ nɖɩ ɖɩtɩkɩlɩ liidiye nɛ ewolo Isilandɩ ɛjaɖɛ taa wayɩ lɛ, ɛlɛ ɛtaahiɣ ɖɩzʋyɛ.
text_en: Couchsurfing was founded in January 2004 after computer programmer Casey Fenton found a cheap flight to Iceland but did not have a place to stay.

text: Etiyini tɔm peeɖe sukuli kɩtɛzʋʋ taa sukulibiya ɛntɛrɩnɛɛtɩ yɔɔ, nɛ ɛyaa sakɩyɛ cosi-i se pahaɣ-ɩ ɖɩzʋyɛ falaa.
text_en: He emailed students at the local university and received an overwhelming number of offers for free accommodation.

text: Maalikasɩ yɔɔdʋʋnɩ kɔzɩ kɔzɩ piya evelisi - yaɖʋ weyi ɛmʋnaa yɔ, ɛwɛnɩ ɛzɩ pɩnzɩ nɛɛlɛ mbʋ yɔ - ɛlɛ nabʋyʋ taa ɩpɩzɩɣ nɛ ɩna nɔmɔʋ wobiyaa mba pa-pɩnzɩ cɛzɩ mbʋ yɔ.
text_en: Hostels cater primarily to young people – a typical guest is in their twenties – but you can often find older travellers there too.

text: Pɩwɛ kaɖɛ se ŋna peeɖe hɔŋ weyi ɩwɛnɩ piya yɔ, ɛlɛ maalikasɩ nasɩyɩ haɣ-wɛ waɖɛ se ɩsʋʋ kɩjaʋ kuduyiŋ nɩɩyɩ taa.
text_en: Families with children are a rare sight, but some hostels do allow them in private rooms.

text: Peekɛɛ tɛtʋ Siini taa, kaɣnɩ kɛʋ tɛtʋ ndʋ tɩ-taa pakaɣ labʋ pɩnaɣ 2022 taa Nikaɣ Alɩwaatʋ taa Ajɛɛ Kɩgbɛndʋʋ Aleɣya yɔ, pɩkaɣ yebu nɛ Peekɛɛ pɩsɩ kajalaɣ tɛtʋ ndʋ tɩ-taa palabɩ soŋaɣ alɩwaatʋ taa ajɛɛ kɩgbɛndʋʋ Aleɣya nɛ pɛtɛ pala nikaɣ alɩwaatʋ taa ñɩna yɔ.
text_en: The city of Beijing in China will be the host city of the Olympic Winter Games in 2022, which will make it the first city to have hosted both the summer and winter Olympics.

text: Beyijiini tɛtʋ taa pakaɣ labʋ aleɣya ana a-nɔɔ tʋlʋʋ nɛ a-nɔɔ ɖɩɣʋ sɔnzɩ. Peeɖe ɖɔɖɔ pakaɣ labʋ aleɣya santaɖaŋ weyi palakɩ ɖɔmbɛ yɔɔ kuduyiŋ tɛɛ yɔɔ.
text_en: Beijing will host the opening and closing ceremonies and the indoor ice events.

text: Pakaɣ labʋ sikii aleɣya lɛɛna Tayizizɛŋg lona wena a-taa papɩzɩɣ nɛ pala sikii yɔ, Zaŋgɩjiyaaku tɛtʋ ndʋ tiposini Peekɛɛ ɛzɩ kilomɛtanaa 220 (mileswaa 140) mbʋ yɔ yɔ.
text_en: Other skiing events will be at the Taizicheng ski area in Zhangjiakou, about 220 km (140 miles) from Beijing.

text: Paa Ɛsɔ sɛtʋ kpaaŋ ŋgʋ lɛ kɩ-taa, palakɩ pɩnaɣ taa kazandʋ natʋyʋ kpaɣnɩ kamɩŋ fenaɣ nɛ piwolo agoza fenaɣ hɛkʋ taa, nɛ pɩlɩɩnɩ paa kpaaŋ ŋgʋ kɩ-alɩwaatʋ ɖʋtʋ yɔɔ lɛ, alɩwaatʋ ndʋ tɩpɩzɩɣ nɛ tɩlɛɣzɩ.
text_en: Most of the temples do have an Annual festival starting from November end to Mid of May, which varies according to each temple's annual calendar.

text: Kpaamɩŋ kazandʋ ndʋ, pɔtɔkɩ tɩ-taa sakɩyɛ ɛzɩ kpaaŋ lʋlʋʋ kazandʋ yaa ɛsɔ weyi ɛwɛ kpaaŋ ŋgʋ kɩ-taa yɔ ɛ-lʋlʋʋ kazandʋ yɔ, yaa lɛɛbʋ mbʋ payɩ pɩkɛ sɔsɔm nɛ pɩlakɩ nɔɔ kʋɖʋmaɣ nɛ kpaaŋ ŋgʋ yɔ.
text_en: Most of the temple festivals is celebrated as part of temple's anniversary or presiding deity's birthday or any other major event associated with the temple.

text: Keralaa tɛtʋ taa kɛ paaŋ kazandʋ wɛ cɔnaʋ pɩdɩɩfɛyɩ, ɖɩnaɣ pɩ-taa tuŋ weyi pacanɩ-ɩ yɔ ɛ-canɖaŋ, kpaaŋ taa soo nɛ kazandʋ lɛɛtʋ.
text_en: Kerala's temple festivals are very interesting to see, with regular procession of decorated elephants, temple orchestra and other festivities.

text: Ɛjaɖɛ kpeekpe yɔɔ wondu pɛdʋʋ kɩyakʋ (ŋgʋ payaɣ ɖoŋ ɖoŋ se kedeŋa kpeekpe yɔɔ wondu wɩlʋʋ, yaa kɛlɛʋ yem se Expo yɔ) kɛ ɛjaɖɛ kpeekpe yɔɔ ajana wondu nɛ lɛɣtʋ ñɩnʋʋ kazandʋ sɔsɔtʋ.
text_en: A World's Fair (commonly called World Exposition, or simply Expo) is large international festival of arts and sciences.

text: Ajɛya wena awoki kazandʋ ndʋ yɔ awɩlɩɣ a-ajana wondu nɛ a-sukuli wɩlʋʋ wondu a-ɛjaɖɛ kpoŋ taa, se pɩsa nɛ alɩzɩ nɛ awɩlɩ kala wena ɛyaa katɩɣ ɛjaɖɛ kpeekpe yɔɔ yɔ, a-sɔnzɩ nɛ a-ɛjaɖɛ taa tɔm.
text_en: Participating countries present artistic and educational displays in national pavilions to showcase world issues or their country's culture and history.

text: Ɛjaɖɛ kpeekpe yɔɔ saɖɩñɛnaa wondu ndʋ palɩzɩɣ nɛ pawɩlʋʋ yɔ, pɩkɛ mbʋ pɩwɛ ŋgee yɔ, nɛ pɩ-taa palɩzɩɣ wondu ndɩ ndɩ nɛ pawɩlɣ ɛzɩ hɛtʋ, tɩŋ hɛtʋ kaɖasɩ nɛ mbʋ payɩ pitukuuni tɩŋ yɔ.
text_en: International Horticultural Expositions are specialised events which showcase floral displays, botanical gardens and anything else to do with plants.

text: Paa paɖʋwa se palakɩ-tʋ paa pɩnaɣ ŋga kɔyɔ (pɩtɩɩñɩtaa pɩla se pɛlɛɣzɩɣ ajɛya yɔ), toovenim taa lɛ paalakɩ mbʋ.
text_en: Although in theory they can take place annually (so long as they are in different countries), in practice they are not.

text: Pɩ-tɩŋa payɩ mbʋ yɔ pɩlabʋ kpakɩɣ ɛzɩ fenasɩ naadozo nɛ piwolo loɖo mbʋ yɔ, nɛ palakɩ-pʋ lona wena a-walanzɩ cɛzɩ ɛkɩtaarɩwaa 50 yɔɔ yɔ.
text_en: These events normally last anywhere between three and six months, and are held on sites no smaller than 50 hectares.

text: Pɩnzɩ wɛɛ nɛ sɩɖɛɣ lɛ, palabɩnɩ filimwaa paɣlɩka ndɩ ndɩ tɔmɩyɛ. Filim ŋgʋ kɩ-paɣlɩka maɣnɩ milimɛtawaa 35 (kizuu taa 36×24 mm) yɔ, ŋgʋ kɩlɩnɩ tɔyʋʋ.
text_en: There are many different film formats that have been used over the years. Standard 35 mm film (36 by 24 mm negative) is much the commonest.

text: Ɖoŋ ɖoŋ lɛ yee ɩfɛyɩnɩ-kʋ yɔ, papɩzɩɣ nɛ palabɩ-mɩ kʋ kɛlɛʋ yem nɛ kɩ-paɣlɩka pɩzɩɣ nɛ kɛwɛɛ ɛzɩ alɩwaatʋ tʋnɛ tɩ-taa fotonaa lɩzʋʋ menziini yɔ.
text_en: It can usually be replenished fairly easily if you run out, and gives resolution roughly comparable to a current DSLR.

text: Fotonaa menziiniwaa nabɛyɛ mba pa-taa wɛ liidiye ñɩɣlɩm pazɩ nɛ po-fotonaa paɣlɩka maɣna yɔ, palakɩnɩ tʋmɩyɛ paɣlɩka santimɛtɛnaa 6 yɔɔ 6, kɔzɩ kɔzɩ miliimɛtawaa 56 yɔɔ 56 kizuu taa.
text_en: Some medium-format film cameras use a 6 by 6 cm format, more precisely a 56 by 56 mm negative.

text: Pʋyɔɔ papaɣlɩ tam naanza nɛ pɩkɩlɩ 35 mm kizuu taa ñɩŋgʋ (milimɛtawaa 3136 tam nabʋlɛ, ndɩ nɛ 864).
text_en: This gives resolution almost four times that of a 35 mm negative (3136 mm2 versus 864).

text: Laŋ taa kpɩna fotonaa lɩzʋʋ kɛnɩ mbʋ pɩwɛ kaɖɛ fotonaa lɩzɩyʋ yɔ. Pʋpɔzʋʋ-ɩ se ɛwɛɛnɩ ñʋʋ leleŋ, suɖuu, menziiniwaa kɩbama nɛ tʋmɩyɛ lɛɣtʋ alɩwaatʋ kʋɖʋmtʋ taa.
text_en: Wildlife is among the most challenging motifs for a photographer, and needs a combination of good luck, patience, experience and good equipment.

text: Ɖoŋ ɖoŋ lɛ pakpakɩɣ kpɩna fotonaa lɩzʋʋ ɛzɩ mbʋ pɩwɛ kɛlɛʋ yɔ, ɛlɛ ɛzɩ fotonaa lalaa yɔ, foto kʋɖʋmʋʋ yɔɔ tɔm pee pɩzɩɣ nɛ atalɩ kudoku.
text_en: Wildlife photography is often taken for granted, but like photography in general, a picture is worth a thousand words.

text: Kpɩna fotonaa lɩzʋʋ pɔzʋʋ nabʋyʋ taa fotonaa nimaɣ kɩɖaalaɣ, paa wondu lɛɛtʋ ɛzɩ sumasɩ tikaɣ yaa kpɩnɛ cikpeɖe ññɩɩɩ naɖɩyɛ ɛpɔzʋʋ nimaɣ lɛɛka kɔyɔ.
text_en: Wildlife photography often requires a long telephoto lens, though things like a flock of birds or a tiny creature need other lenses.

text: Pɩwɛ kaɖɛ se ɛyʋ ɛna agbaɣdaa kpɩna sakɩyɛ, nɛ nabʋyʋ taa kaɖɩsɩ ɖʋʋ paɣtʋ fotonaa lɩzʋʋ nɛ pɛdʋʋ yɔɔ.
text_en: Many exotic animals are hard to find, and parks sometimes have rules about taking photographs for commercial purposes.

text: Tɛtɛgbɩna pɩzɩɣ awɛɛ hɛɛɛ yaa ala ñam ñam lakasɩ. Ɛjaɖɛ yɔɔ pɩzɩɣ pɩwɛɛ nikaɣ, soŋaɣ yaa pɩwɛɛ kaɖɛ se ɛyʋ ɛñɔtɩna.
text_en: Wild animals might either be shy or aggressive. The environment might be cold, hot, or otherwise hostile.

text: Kʋnʋmɩŋ ndɩ ndɩ weyi pɔyɔɔdʋʋ ɛjaɖɛ kpeekpe yɔɔ yɔ, ɛcɛzɩ 5000. Pakpaɣ ɩ-taa nɛɛlɛ yɔ, ɛyaa miiliyɔɔwaa 50 nɛ pɩɖɛɛ pʋ-yɔɔ yɔɔdʋʋnɩ paa kʋnʋŋ ŋgʋ lɛ.
text_en: The world has over 5,000 different languages, including more than twenty with 50 million or more speakers.

text: Tɔm pee wena pamaa yɔ, pɩwɛ kɛlɛʋ se panɩɩ a-taa nɛ pɩkɩlɩ wena pɔyɔɔdaa yɔ. Pɩkɛ toovenim kɔzɩ kɔzɩ adɩrɛɛsɩwaa hɔɔlʋʋ taa mba ɖoŋ ɖoŋ lɛ, pa-yaʋ wɛ kaɖɛ yɔ.
text_en: Written words are often easier to understand than spoken words, also. This is especially true of addresses, which are often difficult to pronounce intelligibly.

text: Ajɛya pilim sakɩyɛ yɔɔdʋʋ anglɛɛ kʋnʋŋ kpayɩ kpayɩ. Ɛlɛ ɩtɩlɩ ɩsɩɩ se nabɛyɛ kaɣ wɛnaʋ tɩlɩtʋ ndʋ tɩwɛnɩ kamaɣ - kɔzɩ kɔzɩ piya evelisi.
text_en: Many entire nations are completely fluent in English, and in even more you can expect a limited knowledge - especially among younger people.

text: Yee ɩsɔɔlaa kɔyɔ, ɩmaɣzɩ se Manɩsɛsɩtɛɛrɩ tʋ nɔɔyʋ, Bostoonii tʋ, Jamayiki tʋ nɛ Sidinee tʋ nɔɔyʋ pacaɣ pa-tɩŋa taabɩlɩ nakʋyʋ yɔɔ kpɛɛɛ nɛ pɔtɔkɩ ɖanaɣ tɔɔnaɣ Torontoo tɔɔnaɣ ɖɩtɔɔyɛ naɖɩyɛ taa.
text_en: Imagine, if you will, a Mancunian, Bostonian, Jamaican and Sydneysider sitting around a table having dinner at a restaurant in Toronto.

text: Pɛkɛdɩɣ ɖama tɛtʋ sɔsɔtʋ ndʋ tɩ-taa palɩnaa tɩ-tɔm, nɛ pɔyʋʋdʋʋnɩ pɛ-tɛtʋ taa nzʋlʋma ndɩ ndɩ nɛ po-kookasɩ taa yɔɔdasɩ.
text_en: They're regaling each other with stories from their hometowns, told in their distinct accents and local argot.

text: Ɖoŋ ɖoŋ lɛ faɣlɛɛ sɔsɔna taa tɔɔnaɣ yabʋ yɔɔ ɛyʋ pɩzɩɣ nɛ ɛtɩŋna kɛlɛʋ nɛ ɛtɔɔ tɔɔnaɣ, nɛ ɛhɛyɩ liidiye ññɩɩ yem. Yee ɛɛpɩzɩɣ se ɛtɩzɩ ɛ-maɣmaɣ ɛ-ɖɩɣa kɔyɔ, tɔɔnasɩ nzɩ pɛtɛm tɩzʋʋ yɔ ɛpɩzɩɣ nɛ ɛya.
text_en: Buying food in supermarkets is usually the cheapest way to get fed. Without cooking opportunities, choices are however limited to ready-made food.

text: Faɣlɛɛ sɔsɔna tɩzɩɣ tɔɔnasɩ ndɩ ndɩ nɛ pɩkɩlɩɣ. Halɩ faɣlɛɛ sɔsɔna naayɛ cɛlɩɣ ɛyaa ñɩɣyʋʋ ŋgʋ kɩ-taa panɩzɩɣ tɔɔnasɩ yɔ yaa nʋmɔŋ lɛɛŋ weyi ɩ-yɔɔ papɩzɩɣ patɩŋna nɛ panɩzɩɣ-kɛ yɔ.
text_en: Increasingly supermarkets are getting a more varied section of ready-made food. Some even provide a microwave oven or other means to heat food.

text: Ajɛya naayɛ yaa maŋgaazɩɩwaa nabɛyɛ taa, tɔɔnaɣ ɖɩpɛdɩyɛ nɖɩ ɖɩwɛ ɖɩ-tɩ yɔɔ yɔ, ɖɩpɛdɩɣ tɔɔnasɩ liidiye taɣyɛɛ.
text_en: In some countries or types of stores there is at least one on-site restaurant, often a rather informal one with affordable prices.

text: Ɩla nɛ ɩkpɛndɩnɩ mɩ-yɔɔ mɩ-paɣtʋ takayɩsɩ nɛ weyi ɛcɔŋnɩ mɩ-tɛ Assurance yɔɔ yɔ ɛ-masɩ.
text_en: Make and carry copies of your policy and your insurer's contact details with you.

text: Pʋcɔ nɛ patasɩ-wɛ lɔŋ/paha-wɛ wala naayɛ nɛ papɩzɩ ɖɔɖɔ nɛ pɔpɔzɩ nabʋyʋ lɛ, pɩcɛyaa se pawɩlɩ pɛ-tɛ Assurance yɔɔ cɔnɩyʋ tɛ ɛntɛrɩnɛɛtɩ lona nɛ ɛ-ajɛya lɛɛna taa kaŋgalaafu masɩ
text_en: They need to show the insurer's e-mail address and international phone numbers for advice/authorizations and making claims.

text: Pɩwɛɛ se ɩwɛɛna takayaɣ lɛzʋʋ lɛɛkʋ mi-wondu taa nɛ ɛntɛrɩnɛɛtɩ yɔɔ (itiyini mɩ-maɣmaɣ mɩ-tɩ nabʋyʋ mɩ-ɛntɛrɩnɛɛtɩ lone yɔɔ, yaa ɩsɩɩ-pʋ "cloud" taa).
text_en: Have another copy in your luggage and online (e-mail to yourself with attachment, or stored in the "cloud").

text: Yee ɩkpɛndɩnɩ mɩ-nʋmɔʋ ɖɔm taa nesi tɛɛ ordinatɛɛrɩ yaa taablɛɛtɩ kɔyɔ, ɩsɩɩ takayaɣ ŋga kɛ-lɛzʋʋ nakʋyʋ pɩ-taa peeɖe (ɩpɩzɩɣ nɛ ɩtʋlɩ-kɛ paa ɛntɛrɩnɛɛtɩ ɛfɛyɩ kɔyɔ).
text_en: If traveling with a laptop or tablet, store a copy in its memory or disc (accessible without the internet).

text: Ɩcɛlɩ ɖɔɖɔ mɩ-paɣtʋ takayɩsɩ lɛzɩŋ/yaa taabalaa mba mɩ nɛ wɛ iwoki nɔmɔʋ, mɩ-lʋlɩyaa nɛ taabalaa mba papɩzɩɣ nɛ pasɩnɩ kpɛdɛyɛ yɔ pa-masɩ.
text_en: Also give policy/contact copies to traveling companions and relatives or friends back home willing to help.

text: Moose (kpɩnɛ nɖɩ payaɣ ɖɔɖɔ se ñɩtʋ taa pʋnʋ sɔsɔ yɔ) fɛyɩ mʋzʋŋ ɖɩ-tɩ yɔɔ, ɛlɛ yee pɛkpɛzɩ-ɖɩ yɔ, ɖɩlʋkɩ ɖɩ-tɩ yɔɔ.
text_en: Moose (also known as elk) aren't inherently aggressive, but will defend themselves if they perceive a threat.

text: Yee ɛyaa ɩmaɣzɩɣ se ñɩtʋ taa pʋŋ sɔsɔŋ fɛyɩ kañatʋ nɛ pɔñɔtɩ pa-tɩ nɛ wɛ kpam kɔyɔ, papɩzɩɣ paɖʋ pa-tɩ kaɖɛ wɛtʋ taa.
text_en: When people don't see moose as potentially dangerous, they may approach too closely and put themselves at risk.

text: Ɩtaaɖɛlɛsɩ sʋlʋm kɩbɩbɩm ñɔʋ. Sʋlʋm fɛyɩnɩ ɖoŋ kʋɖʋmɩŋ ɛyaa tɩŋa yɔɔ, nɛ pɩcɛyaa siŋŋ se ɩtɩlɩ mɩ-kamaɣ.
text_en: Drink alcoholic drinks with moderation. Alcohol affects everyone differently, and knowing your limit is very important.

text: Ɛyʋ ɛñɔʋ sʋlʋm kadadayaɣ yɔ, kʋdɔmɩŋ weyi ɩpɩzɩɣ ɛkpa-ɩ nɛ ɛsɩndaa yɔ, ɩ-taa nɩɩyɩ lɛ hɔyɛ wɛɛkʋʋ, halɩ pɩpɩzɩɣ pɩkɔna yʋlʋnzɩ nɛ sɩm. Nɛ yee potipuu sʋlʋm mbʋ camɩyɛ yɔ, Kala ana apɩzɩɣ akpa ɖoŋ nɛ pɩkɩlɩ.
text_en: Possible long term health events from excessive drinking can include liver damage and even blindness and death. The potential danger is increased when consuming illegally produced alcohol.

text: Sʋlʋm kɩdɛkɛdɩm taa pɩzɩɣ pɩwɛɛ kʋzɔɔtʋ ndɩ ndɩ ndʋ tɩkɔŋnɩ kala yɔ, ɛzɩ metaanɔɔlɩ ŋgʋ, paa ɛyʋ ɛñɔ-kʋ ŋñɩɩ yem kana yɔ, kɩpɩzɩɣ kɩha-ɩ yʋlʋnzɩ nɛ halɩ sɩm.
text_en: Illegal spirits can contain various dangerous impurities including methanol, which can cause blindness or death even in small doses.

text: Ɛsɩñɩnɩŋ pɩzɩɣ ɩɩwɛɣ liidiye agbaɣdaa ɛjaɖɛ naɖɩyɛ taa, kɔzɩ kɔzɩ kʋñɔndʋtʋ ajɛya taa, ɖenɖe paahɛyɩɣ ɛyaa liidiye sakɩyɛ pa-tʋma yɔɔ yɔ.
text_en: Eyeglasses can be cheaper in a foreign country, especially in low-income countries where labour costs are lower.

text: Ɩla ɖʋtʋ nɛ pɔkɔɔ pamaɣzɩ mɩ-ɛsa mɩ-ɖɩɣa, kɔzɩ kɔzɩ yee ɩwɛnɩ Assurance kɔyɔ. Ɩtaasɔɔ se ɩkpɛndɩna takayaɣ ŋga kɔ-yɔɔ pama yɔ nɛ paatɛzɩ-kɛ ɖom lɛɛɖɛ.
text_en: Consider getting an eye exam at home, especially if insurance covers it, and bringing the prescription along to be filed elsewhere.

text: Wondu ndʋ pasɩm-tʋ se tɩwɛ ɖeu nɛ tɩwɛɛ tɛtʋ hɔɔlɩŋ ɩnɩ ɩ-taa yɔ, tɩpɩzɩɣ tɩkatɩ kala naalɛ : natʋyʋ pɩzɩɣ nɛ tɩkɛ kɩbandʋ lɛzɩŋ yem, nɩ ndʋ tʋtʋ ñɛkɛ kɩbandʋ yɔ, tɩpɩzɩɣ nɛ tɩwɛɛ liidiye ɖɛ-tɛ nɛ pɩkɩlɩ.
text_en: High-end brand-name frames available in such areas may have two problems; some may be knock-offs, and the real imported ones may be more expensive than at home.

text: Wondu ndʋ pakɩlɩɣ pɛdʋʋ ɛjɛɖɛ kpeekpe yɔɔ yɔ, tɩ-taa natʋyʋ lɛ kɔfɩ, nɛ hɔɔlʋʋ ŋgʋ kɩ-taa ɩwɛɛ yɔ, ɩpɩzɩɣ nɛ ɩna kɔfɩnaa ndɩ ndɩ.
text_en: Coffee is one of the world's most traded commodities, and you can probably find many types in your home region.

text: Paa mbʋ yɔ, kɔfɩ ñɔʋ wɛ ndɩ ndɩ ɛjɛɖɛ kpeekpe yɔɔ, nɛ pɩwɛɣ ɖeu se ɩmaɣzɩ-pʋ nɛ ɩna.
text_en: Nevertheless, there are many distinctive ways of drinking coffee around the world that are worth experiencing.

text: Aleɣya wena payaɣ se canyoning (yaa : canyonisme) yɔ a-taa, ɛyaa tiki pɔʋ ŋgʋ lɩm huyaa yɔ kɩ-taa, paa lɩm ɛwɛ kɩ-taa yaa pɩfɛyɩ kɔyɔ.
text_en: Canyoning (or: canyoneering) is about going in a bottom of a canyon, which is either dry or full of water.

text: Canyoning aleɣya taa, pɛkpɛndɩɣ lɩm yaʋ, kpaʋ nɛ maʋ; ɛlɛ pɩtɩcɛyɩ se ɛyʋ ɛhayɩsɩ ɛ-tɩ sakɩyɛ yaa ɛwɛɛ ɖoŋ sakɩyɛ pʋcɔ nɛ ɛpaɣzɩ a-labʋ (pɩwɛ ndɩ nɛ pʋŋ kpaʋ, teŋgu tɛɛ tibu yaa pʋʋ taa sikii labʋ mbʋ yɔ).
text_en: Canyoning combines elements from swimming, climbing and jumping--but requires relatively little training or physical shape to get started (compared to rock climbing, scuba diving or alpine skiing, for example).

text: Heelim mʋʋ ɖɔnɛ kɛ aleɣya wena palakɩ-yɛ yem fɛɛɛ yɔ; a-taa lɛ, ɛyaa yɛlʋʋ lona ndɩ ndɩ taa, nɛ ɖoŋ ɖoŋ lɛ pɔɖɔŋ nɔmɔʋ ŋgʋ nʋmɔsɔkasɩ taa.
text_en: Hiking is an outdoor activity which consists of walking in natural environments, often on hiking trails.

text: Evemiye taa nʋmɔʋ ɖɔm pɩzɩɣ pɩɖaalɩ ɛzɩ mɛtanaa 1609 mbʋ yɔ nɛ halɩ pɩpɩzɩɣ pɩɖaalɩ pɩkɩlɩ mbʋ.
text_en: Day hiking involves distances of less than a mile up to longer distances that can be covered in a single day.

text: Yee pɔɖɔŋ evemiye taa nɔmɔʋ nʋmɔsɔka ŋga kɔ-yɔɔ kaɖɛ naɖɩyɛ fɛyɩ kɔyɔ, pɩtɩcɛyɩ se ɛyʋ ɛñɔɔzɩ ɛ-tɩ sakɩyɛ, nɛ paa ɛyʋ ɛfɛyɩ ɖoŋ sakɩyɛ yɔ, ɛpɩzɩɣ nɛ ɛfanɩ waɖɛ nɖɩ.
text_en: For a day hike along an easy trail little preparations are needed, and any moderately fit person can enjoy them.

text: Hɔŋ weyi ɩ-taa piya evelisi nɛ piya ajama wɛɛ yɔ, pɩpɩzɩɣ nɛ pʋpɔzɩ-ɩ tɩ-ñʋʋzʋʋ nɛ pɩkɩlɩ. Ɛlɛ papɩzɩɣ palɩɩ evemiye pilim nɛ awayɩ paa pɛwɛnɩ piya cɩɩɩ waa yaa piya ajama kɔyɔ.
text_en: Families with small children may need more preparations, but a day outdoors is easily possible even with babies and pre-school children.

text: Kedeŋa kpeekpe yɔɔ, heelim mʋʋ agbaa wena aɖiɣni tʋmɩyɛ labʋ yɔ, añɔtɩnɩ 200. A-taa sakɩyɛ lakɩ tʋmɩyɛ a-tɩ yɔɔ.
text_en: Internationally, there are nearly 200 running tour organizations. Most of them operate independently.

text: Ɛgbɛyɛ nɖɩ ɖɩlɛɣzɩ Global Running Tours lone taa nɛ payaɣ-ɖɩ se Go Running Tours yɔ, kedenzi naanza taa, ɖɩlakɩ tʋmɩyɛ nɔɔ kʋɖʋmaɣ nɛ tʋmlaɖaa mba pɛpɛdɩɣ seya wondu yɔ, pa-taa hiŋ sakɩyɛ.
text_en: The Global Running Tours successor, Go Running Tours networks dozens of sightrunning providers on four continents.

text: Seya wena ɛgbɛyɛ nɖɩ, ɖɩlabɩ Running Tours Barcelona taa Barcelɔɔnɩ tɛtʋ taa, nɛ Running Copenhague taa Kopɛnhaagɩ tɛtʋ taa yɔ, ayeba nɛ kpɛdɛyɛ taa lɛ Running Tours Prague, ɛgbɛyɛ nɖɩ ɖɩwɛ Pɩraagɩ, nɛ agbaa lɛɛna, pɔsɔzɩ ɖɩ-yɔɔ.
text_en: With roots in Barcelona's Running Tours Barcelona and Copenhagen's Running Copenhagen, it was quickly joined by Running Tours Prague based in Prague and others.

text: Pɩwɛɛ se ɩmaɣzɩ wondu sakɩyɛ yɔɔ pʋcɔ nɛ alɩwaatʋ ndʋ iwoki nɔmɔʋ ɖoli yɔ tɩtalɩ.
text_en: There are many things you have to take into consideration before and when you travel somewhere.

text: Alɩwaatʋ ndʋ iwoki nɔmɔʋ yɔ, ɩtɩlɩ ɛsɩɩ se pɩ-tɩŋa pɩɩkaɣ wɛʋ ɛzɩ pɩwɛʋ "mɩ-tɛ" yɔ. Sɔnzɩ, paɣtʋ, tɔɔnaɣ, habɩyɛ yɔɔ ɖɔnɛ, ɖɩzʋyɛ, paɣtʋ kila, nɛ lɛɛbʋ mbʋ yɔ, pɩkaɣ nabʋyʋ taa wɛʋ ndɩ nɛ ɖenɖe ɩwɛɛ yɔ.
text_en: When you travel, expect things not to be like they are "back home". Manners, laws, food, traffic, lodging, standards, language and so on will to some extent differ from where you live.

text: Pɩkɛ mbʋ pʋpɔzʋʋ se pɩwɛɛ mɩ-ñʋŋ taa tam yɔ, se pɩtaakɔɔ nɛ pitibi-mɩ yɔɔɔ yaa ɛzɩma ɛyaa lakɩ ɖenɖe iwoki yɔ, pɩtaakɔɔ nɛ pɩlɩɩ-mɩ sɔŋ.
text_en: This is something you always need to keep in mind, to avoid disappointment or perhaps even distaste over local ways to do things.

text: Kpaɣnɩ waɣ 19 ñɩŋga taa nʋmɔʋ wobu agbaa ñɔwa. Doŋ ɖoŋ lɛ, pɩpɔzɩɣ-ɩ nɔmɔʋ wobu ɛgbɛyɛ taa tʋmlaɖʋ nɔɔyʋ tɛ sɩnaʋ, yee nɔmɔʋ woɖu ɛsɔɔlaa se ɛnɩɩ leleŋ ɛ-nʋmɔʋ taa nɛ pɩkɩlɩ nʋmaŋ weyi ɛɛtɛm wobu, pɩtɩɩkɛ ɛjɛɖɛ wɛtʋ, sɔnzɩ, kʋnʋŋ yaa ajɛya wena a-taa paahɛyɩɣ tʋmlaɖaa liidiye sakɩyɛ yɔ, pʋ-hɔɔlʋʋ taa kɔyɔ.
text_en: Travel agencies have been around since the 19th century. A travel agent is usually a good option for a journey which extends beyond a traveller's previous experience of nature, culture, language or low-income countries.

text: Paa agbaa sakɩyɛ ɩsɔɔlɩ faaa se amʋ a-hazasɩ yɔɔ nʋmɔʋ ɖɩjaɣyɛ kazʋʋ taa sakɩyɛ yɔ, nʋmɔʋ agbaa taa tʋmlaɖaa sakɩyɛ kaŋ pa-ñʋŋ nɛ ŋgee nʋmaŋ wobu nɩɩyɩ, liidiye tamasɩ nasɩyɩ labʋ yaa lona naayɛ taa wobu.
text_en: Although most agencies are willing to take on most regular bookings, many agents specialise in particular types of travel, budget ranges or destinations.

text: Pɩpɩzɩɣ pɩwɛɛ weewee nɛ pɩkɩlɩ se nʋmɔʋ wobu ɛgbɛyɛ taa tʋmlaɖʋ weyi ɛkazɩɣ ɛyaa ɖɩjaɣyɛ nɛ pɩlakɩ nɔɔ kʋɖʋmaɣ nɛ mɩ-nʋmɔʋ yɔ, ɛnʋ ɛsɩnɩnɩ-mɩ.
text_en: It can be better to use an agent who frequently books similar trips to yours.

text: Ɩyaɣ ɛsɩyɛ nʋmaŋ weyi ɛgbɛyɛ taa tʋmlaɖʋ seɣtiɣ ɛyaa se powolo yɔ ɩ-yɔɔ nɛ ɩna, paa pɩtɩɩkɛ ɛntɛrɩnɛɛtɩ lone naɖɩyɛ yɔɔ yaa wondu ɖɩzɩyɛ naɖɩyɛ taa kɔyɔ.
text_en: Take a look at what trips the agent is promoting, whether on a website or in a shop window.

text: Yee ɛsɔɔlaa se ɩyɛlɩ ɛjaɖɛ yɔɔ nɛ ɩhɛyɩ liidiye pazɩ yem, ye pɩkɛnɩ-mɩ kɩjɛyʋʋ, yaa mi-wezuu caɣʋ wɛtʋ ɛpɔzʋʋna mbʋ, yaa ɩɖʋ mɩ-tɩ kaɖʋwa nakɛyɛ kɩɖʋʋ kɔyɔ, ɩpɩzɩɣ ɩtɩŋnɩ nʋmaŋ sakɩyɛ yɔɔ nɛ ɩla mbʋ.
text_en: If you want to see the world on the cheap, for necessity, lifestyle or challenge, there are some ways to do that.

text: Ɖeyi ɖeyi lɛ, papɩzɩɣ patayɩ-wɛ hɔɔlɩŋ naalɛ taa : ɩpɩzɩɣ nɛ iɖiɣni tʋmɩyɛ labʋ alɩwaatʋ ndʋ ɩwɛ mɩ-nʋmɔʋ wobu taa yɔ, yaa ɩpɩzɩɣ ɩñaɣ pana nɛ ɩtaakɩlɩ mi-liidiye wɛɛkʋʋ. Kɛdɛzaɣ hɔɔlʋʋ kʋnɛ kɩ-yɔɔ takayaɣ kanɛ kakaŋ ñʋʋ
text_en: Basically, they fall into two categories: Either work while you travel or try and limit your expenses. This article is focused on the latter.

text: Mba pɔsɔɔlɩ faaa se pakpaɣ ɖɩɣa taa hɛzɩyɛ, alɩwaatʋ nɛ tɩ ñɔɔzʋʋ nɛ palaa kɩlaʋ se pɩsa nɛ pataahɛyɩ liidiye sakɩyɛ yɔ, ɩtasɩ kalʋʋ nʋmɔʋ wobu liidiye nɖɩ pʋpɔzʋʋ kpidikpidi yɔ,  ɖɩ-yɔɔ tɔm.
text_en: For those willing to sacrifice comfort, time and predictability to push expenses down close to zero, see minimum budget travel.

text: Lɔŋ tasɩyaa taɣ liu se nɔmɔʋ woɖaa ɩɩmɩlɩɣ, paasʋʋ yem yem, ɩɩyakɩ cɛtɩm kɩyakɩŋ, paasʋlʋmʋʋ yaa paamuluu lalaa se pehiɣ pa-maɣmaɣ pɛ-kɛzɛsɩ.
text_en: The advice assumes that travellers do not steal, trespass, participate in the illegal market, beg, or otherwise exploit other people for their own gain.

text: Ɖoŋ ɖoŋ lɛ, lone nɖɩ ɖɩ-taa pewiliɣ mba pɛlɛɣzɩɣ ɛjaɖɛ yaa tɛtʋ yɔ, peeɖe lɔɔɖa, mɛlɛnaa yaa ɛsɔdaa lɔɔɖa calɩɣ sɩŋʋʋ se ɛyaa itii.
text_en: An immigration checkpoint is usually the first stop when disembarking from a plane, a ship, or another vehicle.

text: Sulukiŋ weyi ɩtɛzɩɣ kamasɩ yɔ ɩ-taa nɩɩyɩ taa, pewiliɣ ɛyaa alɩwaatʋ ndʋ suluku ɖiɣni ɖɔm yɔ nɛ pɩkɛnɩ kɩjɛyʋʋ se pʋcɔ nɛ ŋkpa suluku taa lɛ,  ŋwɛɛna ña-takayaɣ ŋga katɩsɩbɩta yɔ ñɔ-yɔɔ.
text_en: In some cross-border trains inspections are done on the running train and you should have valid ID with you when boarding one of those trains.

text: Sulukiŋ weyi ɩɖɔŋ ɖoo taa yɔ ɩ-taa, suluku sayʋ pɩzɩɣ nɛ ɛmʋ mɩ-takayaɣ ŋga kahaɣ-mɩ waɖɛ se ɩtɛzɩ kamasɩ yɔ, se pɩsa nɛ pataafezi-mɩ pʋwayɩ se pʋcɔ pamʋ-kɛ.
text_en: On night sleeper trains, passports may be collected by the conductor so that you do not have your sleep interrupted.

text: Hɩɖɛ maʋ kɛ ɖɔɖɔ mbʋ pɩ-tɔm cɛyaa pʋcɔ nɛ pala ɛyʋ ɛjaɖɛ lɛɛɖɛ taa wobu takayaɣ yɔ. Ajɛya naayɛ taa lɛ, pʋpɔzʋʋ se iwolo ñʋndɩnaa cɔlɔ nɛ payʋsɩ alɩwaatʋ ɛzɩma ɩcakɩ peeɖe nɛ mi-kuduyuu mayaɣ.
text_en: Registration is an additional requirement for the visa process. In some countries, you must register your presence and address where you are staying with the local authorities.

text: Pɩpɩzɩɣ nɛ pɩpɔzɩ se iwolo polisinaa cɔlɔ nɛ payʋsɩ takayaɣ nakɛyɛ, yaa iwolo ɛjaɖɛ lɛɣzʋʋ tʋmɩyɛ naɖɩyɛ taa.
text_en: This might require filling out a form with the local police or a visit to the immigration offices.

text: Ajɛɛ wena a-taa paɣtʋ ndʋ tɩwɛɛ yɔ, agɔma ɖɩsɩ maɣna hɩla (ɩtaasɔɔ se ɩpɔzɩ).
text_en: In many countries with such a law, local hotels will handle the registration (make sure to ask).

text: Hɔɔlɩŋ lɛɛŋ taa lɛ, ɛyaa mba pasʋʋ ɖɩsɩ nzɩ sɩtɩkɛ agɔma ɖɩzʋyɛ yɔ, pa-hɩla ɖeke pɩwɛɛ se pama. Piyeki nɛ ɛyaa mba ɩɩtasɩɣ paɣtʋ taa nɩʋ camɩyɛ, pʋyɔɔ lɛ ɩpɔzɩ lɔŋ nɛ pʋcɔ.
text_en: In other cases, only those staying outside of tourist accommodations need to register.  However, this makes the law much more obscure, so find out beforehand.

text: Kuduyiŋ maʋ lɛɣtʋ tukuuni kuduyiŋ lɩmaɣza labʋ nɛ ɩ-maʋ. Lone naɖɩyɛ tɛ kuduyiŋ maʋ lɛɣtʋ pɩzɩɣ nɛ pɩpɩsɩ ɛsɩyɛgbena pʋyʋ.
text_en: Architecture is concerned with the design and construction of buildings. The architecture of a place is often a tourist attraction in its own right.

text: Ŋcɔnɩ kuduyiŋ sakɩyɛ kɔyɔ, ɩwɛ kajʋka pɩdɩɩfɛyɛ, kɔzɩ kɔzɩ yee ŋwɛ kuduyuu sɔsɔʋ nakʋyʋ taa nɛ ŋcɔŋna yɔ, yaa yee ŋsɩŋ mondoɖebɔʋ ŋgʋ kɩtʋʋzɩnɩ kuduyuu ŋgʋ kɔyɔ.
text_en: Many buildings are quite beautiful to look at and the view from a tall building or from a cleverly-positioned window can be a beauty to behold.

text: Kuduyiŋ maʋ lɛɣtʋ makɩɣna ɖɔɖɔ hɔɔlɩŋ lɛɛŋ ɛzɩ tɛtʋ sɔsɔtʋ tʋmɩyɛ, samaɣ kuduyiŋ maʋ tʋmɩyɛ, wondu canʋʋ tʋmɩyɛ, kuduyiŋ taa canʋʋ tʋmɩyɛ, nɛ tɛtʋ ñɔɔzʋʋ tʋmɩyɛ.
text_en: Architecture overlaps considerably with other fields including urban planning, civil engineering, decorative arts, interior design and landscape design.

text: Ɛzɩma tɛtʋ sakɩyɛ posaa yɔ pʋyɔɔ lɛ, yee ŋtɩwolo Alɩbuukɛrɩkɩ yaa Santa Fee tɛtʋ taa kɔyɔ, ŋŋpɩzɩɣ nɛ ŋna ɛyaa ɖoho taa.
text_en: Given how remote many of the pueblos are, you won't be able to find a significant amount of nightlife without traveling to Albuquerque or Santa Fe.

text: Ɛlɛ lotɛri agbaa wena ɖɩyaa nɛ pɩɖɛɛ yɔ, apɛdɩɣ sʋlʋm, nɩ a-taa sakɩyɛ lakɩ aleɣya sɔsɔna (kɔzɩ kɔzɩ agbaa wena acɔ Alɩbuukɛrɩkɩ nɛ Santa Fee kpaagbaa nɛ ata yɔ).
text_en: However, nearly all of the casinos listed above serve drinks, and several of them bring in name-brand entertainment (primarily the large ones immediately surrounding Albuquerque and Santa Fe).

text: Ɩkpa mɩ-tɩ : cɩnɛ, tɛtʋ cikpetu taa sʋlʋm faɣlɛɛ tɩkɛ paa ɛzɩmtaa lona wena a-taa agɔma pɩzɩɣ awolo faaa yɔ.
text_en: Beware: small-town bars here are not always good places for the out-of-state visitor to hang out.

text: Hɔɔlʋʋ nakʋyʋ taa lɛ, Mɛkɩsiiki Kɩfalʋʋ nɛ hayo kiŋ tɛtʋ taa, ɛyaa mba pahaɣ sʋlʋm yɔ ɛlɛ pasaɣ lɔɔɖa pɔtɔyaa pɩdɩɩfɛyɛ, nɛ ŋpɩzɩɣ ŋna-wɛ tɛtʋ cikpetu taa sʋlʋm faɣlɛɛ cɔlɔ.
text_en: For one thing, northern New Mexico has significant problems with drunk driving, and the concentration of intoxicated drivers is high close to small-town bars.

text: Kolonzi yɔɔ tɔlɩm mbʋ pɩpɩnaa yɔ nɛ anjaʋwaa mba paanaɣ camɩyɛ yɔ, ɛyaa kpakɩɣ-wɛ ɛzɩ  graffitiɩ .
text_en: Unwanted murals or scribble is known as graffiti.

text: Paa pɩtɩtɩɩ kɛʋ sɔnɔ pʋyʋ kɔyɔ, ɛyaa maɣzɩɣ se pɩwɛ ɛzɩ piya evelisi kpakɩɣ tɔlɩm nɛ pɛwɛɛkɩɣ ɛyaa nabɛyɛ yaa ɛjaɖɛ kpeekpe ñɩm yɔ.
text_en: While it's far from a modern phenomenon, most people probably associate it with youth vandalizing public and private property using spray paint.

text: Ɛlɛ sɔnɔ, tɔlɩm tayaa nɛ tɔlɩm taʋ ɖʋtʋ ndʋ paɣtʋ haɣ waɖɛ yɔ, tɩwɛɛ. Hɔɔlʋʋ ŋgʋ kɩ-taa lɛ, pɩtɩtasɩ wɛʋ ɛzɩ anjaʋwaa mba paanaɣ camɩyɛ yɔ, ɛlɛ ɛzɩ wondu lɩzʋʋ nɩ tɔlɩm yɔ.
text_en: However, nowadays there are established graffiti artists, graffiti events and "legal" walls. Graffiti paintings in this context often resemble artworks rather than illegible tags.

text: Aleɣya naayɛ taa lɛ, ɛyʋ lɔʋ nabʋyʋ ɛsɔdaa lɛ pʋ-tʋ ɛnʋ ɛpɩsɩ ɛ-cɔlɔ. Nɛ ɛsɩyɛgbena tɩnaa sakɩyɛ sɔɔlaa se patɩlɩ a-labʋ.
text_en: Boomerang throwing is a popular skill that many tourists want to acquire.

text: Yee ŋ-sɔɔlaa se ŋ-kpɛlɩkɩ ɛzɩma ŋlɔ nabʋyʋ nɛ pɩpɩsɩ ñe-nesi taa kɔyɔ, ñɩnɩ mbʋ pɩsɩʋ ɛɛlakɩ-pʋ kaɖɛ yɔ.
text_en: If you want to learn throwing a boomerang that comes back to your hand, make sure you have a suitable boomerang for returning.

text: Ositralii ɛjɛɖɛ taa wondu ndʋ ɛyaa lɔʋ yɔ, tɩ-taa sakɩyɛ ɩɩpɩsɩɣ. Pʋyɔɔ pɩkɩlɩɣ ɖeu se mba pɛkpɛlɩkɩɣ kɩkpɛlɩkʋ yɔ, pataalɔ heelim taa yem.
text_en: Most boomerangs available in Australia are in fact non-returning. It is best for beginners to not try throwing in windy

text: Patɩzɩɣ Haŋgii tɔɔnaɣ tɛtɛɛ pɔʋ sɔsɔʋ nakʋyʋ, ŋgʋ kɩ-taa soŋgaa yɔ, kɩ-taa.
text_en: A Hangi Meal is cooked in a hot pit in the ground.

text: Pɔʋ ŋgʋ papɩzɩɣ posoŋ-kɛ nɛ pɛɛ wena paɖʋ-yɛ miŋ taa yɔ. Lona lɛɛna taa lɛ, tɛtɛɛ hohou mamaɣ soŋguuni pɔŋ ɩnɩ.
text_en: The pit is either heated with hot stones from a fire, or in some places geothermal heat makes areas of ground naturally hot.

text: Palakɩna Haŋgii tʋmɩyɛ ɖoŋ ɖoŋ nɛ patɩzɩɣ ɖanaɣ tɔɔnaɣ, nɛ pɩkɛ tɔɔnaɣ ŋga pawɩsɩɣ kɩwɩsʋ yɔ.
text_en: The hangi is often used to cook a traditional roast style dinner.

text: Rotoruuna tɛtʋ taa lona sakɩyɛ taa, ɖɩnaɣ Haŋgiiwaa mba patɩzɩnɩ tɛtɛɛ hohou yɔ, ɛlɛ papɩzɩɣ pana haŋgiiwaa lalaa Krɩtʋcooci Weeliŋgtɔɔnɩ nɛ lona lɛɛna taa.
text_en: Several places in Rotorua offer geothermal hangi, while other hangi can be sampled in Christchurch, Wellington and elsewhere.

text: Meetroo Raayɩ wɛnɩ ɖamɩŋ naalɛ sulukiŋ weyi ɩwɛ Kaapɩ Tawɩnɩ taa nɛ kɩ-wayɩ yɔ : Meetroo Pliisi (ŋgʋ payaɣ ɖɔɖɔ se First Class yɔ) nɛ Meetroo (payaɣ-kʋ ɖɔɖɔ se Third Class).
text_en: MetroRail has two classes on commuter trains in and around Cape Town: MetroPlus (also called First Class) and Metro (called Third Class).

text: Hɛzɩyɛ wɛ Meetroo Pliisi taa nɛ pɩkɩlɩ nɛ pɩɩñɩɣdʋʋ ɛyʋ, ɛlɛ kɩwɛ liidiye pazɩ nɛ pɩkɩlɩ, paa kɩfɛyɩ liidiye nɛ pɩtalɩ Erɔɔpɩ sulukiŋ tikeenaa kɔyɔ.
text_en: MetroPlus is more comfortable and less crowded but slightly more expensive, though still cheaper than normal metro tickets in Europe.

text: Paa suluku ŋgʋ lɛ, kɩwɛnɩ lɔɔɖa cikpena; payaɣ naayɛ se Meetroo Pliisi nɛ lɛɛna se Meetroo. Wena payaɣ se Meetroo Pliisi yɔ, paa ɛzɩmtaa awɛ suluku ŋgʋ kɩkɩlɩ ñɔtɩnaʋ Kaapɩ Tawɩnɩ yɔ, kɩ-nɔɔ taa.
text_en: Every train has both MetroPlus and Metro coaches; the MetroPlus coaches are always on the end of the train nearest Cape Town.

text: Lalaa wondu sɩɣlʋʋ - Mɩ-ɛsa ɩwɛɛ mi-wondu yɔɔ tam, kɔzɩ kɔzɩ yee ɩtɛzɩɣ ajɛya ndɩ ndɩ kamasɩ kɔyɔ.
text_en: Carrying for others - Never let your bags out of your sight, especially when you are crossing international borders.

text: Nabɛyɛ pɩzɩɣ pasʋʋ-mɩ tabakʋyaɣ ɛlɛ ɩɩnaɣ, nɛ pɩkaɣ-mɩ kɔnʋʋ Kala sakɩyɛ.
text_en: You could find yourself being used as a drug carrier without your knowledge, which will land you in a great deal of trouble.

text: Pɩ-taa lɛ canzɩ pɩlʋʋ wɛɛ, mbʋ pʋyɔɔ yɔ papɩzɩɣ palabɩnɩ tʋmɩyɛ hasɩ nzɩ sɩsɔŋʋʋ se sɩñɩnɩ tabakʋyaɣ yɔ, ɛlɛ paaheyiɣ nɔɔyʋ.
text_en: This includes waiting in line, as drug-sniffing dogs could be used at any time without notice.

text: Pɔhɔŋ ɛyaa nɩŋgbaaŋ siŋŋ ajɛya sakɩyɛ taa, paa kajalaɣ ɖeɖe palabɩ nabʋyʋ nɛ pakpa-wɛ kɔyɔ. Papɩzɩɣ pɔtɔ-wɛ salaka pɩnzɩ ɛzɩ 10 nɛ pɩɖɛɛ pʋ-yɔɔ, yaa papɩzɩɣ nɛ pakʋ-wɛ.
text_en: Some countries have exceedingly draconian punishments even for first time offenses; these can include prison sentences of over 10 years or death.

text: Huyiŋ weyi nɔɔyʋ eekeŋni-i yɔ, papɩzɩɣ nɛ pamɩlɩ-ɩ kɛlɛʋ yem. Huyiŋ ɩnɩ ɩhɔŋ ɖɔɖɔ ñʋndɩnaa lɩmaɣza mbʋ pʋyɔɔ yɔ sɔɔndʋ kpaɣ-wɛ se hɔzɩŋ sɔsɔŋ kaawɛɛ pɩ-taa.
text_en: Unattended bags are a target for theft and can also attract attention from authorities wary of bomb threats.

text: Ɛzɩma kʋdɔmɩŋ pee tɔyɩ ɖɩsɩ taa yɔ pʋ-yɔɔ lɛ, pɩwɛ ɛzɩ pɛtɛm-mɩ  kʋdɔmɩŋ ɩnɩ ɩ-ɖatʋ kɔyɛ sɔnɔ yɔ.
text_en: At home, due to this constant exposure to the local germs, odds are very high that you're already immune to them.

text: Ɛlɛ ajɛya hɔɔlɩŋ lɛɛŋ weyi ɩ-taa ɩkatɩɣ kʋdɔmɩŋ pee kɩfana yɔ ɩ-taa, pɩpɩzɩɣ pɩwɛɛ-mɩ kaɖɛ nɛ pɩkɩlɩ.
text_en: But in other parts of the world, where the bacteriological fauna are new to you, you're far more likely to run into problems.

text: Pɩtasɩ lɛ, ajɛya hɔɔlɩŋ weyi ɩ-taa soŋaɣ wɛɛ yɔ ɩ-taa, kʋdɔmɩŋ pee yɛlɩɣ lɛɛlɛɛ nɛ pɩkɩlɩ, nɛ paa ɩtɩsʋta ɛyʋ tomnaɣ taa kɔyɔ, ɩcakɩ wezuu nɛ pileɖi.
text_en: Also, in warmer climates bacteria both grow more quickly and survive longer outside the body.

text: Mbʋ pɩlɩ Deelii Beelii lakasɩ taa yɔ, nɔɔ kɩdɛkɛdaɣ ŋga Pharaɔɔ lɔwa yɔ, Monteezumaa kɩmɩyɛ kpaʋ, nɛ pa-tabalaa sakɩyɛ.
text_en: Thus the scourges of Delhi Belly, the Pharaoh's Curse, Montezuma's Revenge, and their many friends.

text: Ɛzɩma feziŋ ɩɩtalɩɣ ɛyaa lona wena a-taa wɛ nikaɣ yɔ, mbʋ ɖɔɖɔ lotu taa kʋdɔmɩŋ tɔyɩ ɖenɖe soŋaɣ wɛɛ yɔ. Kʋdɔmɩŋ ɩnɩ ɩcɛyɩɣ ɛyaa ɖoŋ ɖoŋ, ɛlɛ pɩkɔŋna kaɖɛ sakɩyɛ.
text_en: As with respiratory problems in colder climates, intestinal problems in hot climates are fairly common and in most cases are distinctly annoying but not really dangerous.

text: Ye ña-kajalaɣ ɖeɖe ŋwoki kʋñɔndʋtʋ ɛjaɖɛ naɖɩyɛ taa, yaa ɛjaɖɛ hɔɔlʋʋ kɩfalʋʋ nakʋyʋ taa kɔyɔ, tɩlɩ ŋsɩɩ se ŋpɩzɩɣ nɛ ŋkatɩ sɔŋzɩ kɩfasɩ sakɩyɛ.
text_en: If traveling in a developing country for the first time – or in a new part of the world – don't underestimate the potential culture shock.

text: Nɔmɔʋ woɖaa mba papɩzɩɣ, nɛ pɛwɛ pa-tɩ yɔɔ ɖɔɖɔ yɔ, powobi kʋñɔndʋtʋ ajɛya taa nɛ kɩfam mbʋ pakataa yɔ, piyeba nɛ pɩnɩɩ-wɛ; ajɛya ana a-taa, sɔnzɩ wɛtʋ pɩzɩɣ nɛ tɩlɛɣzɩ alɩwaatʋ ŋñɩɩ taa.
text_en: Many a stable, capable traveler has been overcome by the newness of developing world travel, where many little cultural adjustments can add up quickly.

text: Ɩmaɣzɩ sɩ ɩlakɩ kpanzɩɩtʋ nɛ wɩsɩ ɖɩ-ɖʋyɛ tɛ ɖɔnɛ, agɔma kuduyɩŋ kɩpaŋ nɛ kɔyɔka ñɩŋ, tɔɔnaɣ nɛ tʋma sɩ pɩsɩna-mɩ nɛ pɩmalɩnɩ-mɩ.
text_en: Especially in your initial days, consider splurging on Western-style and -quality hotels, food, and services to help acclimatize.

text: Ɩtaaɖoo ñalɩŋ yaa tefeɖinaa yɔɔ tataa kɛ lona wena a-taa ɩɩsɩŋ laʋ nɛ kɩ-wɛtʋ yɔ.
text_en: Do not sleep on a mattress or pad on the ground in areas where you do not know the local fauna.

text: Yee ɩwoki  caɣʋ yɔ, ɩkpendɩna caɣyaa tɛ kaɖʋ yaa kamaka nɛ pɩsa nɩ ɩpɔsi mɩ-tɩ nɛ ɖʋmaa, pɩcɩsɩ nɛ tɛtɛ wondu.
text_en: If you are going to camp out, bring a camp cot or hammock to keep you away from snakes, scorpions and such.

text: Ɩhaɣzɩ mɩ-ɖɩɣa kɔfɩ kɩbaŋgʊ tanaŋ tɛɛ, camaɣ ŋga kalɩzɩɣ ñɩŋgaanzɩ yɔ ɖanaɣ yɔɔ.
text_en: Fill your home with a rich coffee in the morning and some relaxing chamomile tea at night.

text: Alɩwaatʊʊ ndʋ ɩwɛ caɣyɩtʋ yɔ, ɩpɩzɩɣ nɛ ɩkpaɣ alɩwaatʊ natʋyʋ cabɩ nɩ ɩla kɔjɔka nabuyʋ nɛ pɩkɔna-mɩ laŋhʊlʊmɩyɛ nɛ taaa leleŋ.
text_en: When you're on a staycation, you have the time to treat yourself and take a few extra minutes to brew up something special.

text: Yee ɩñɔyɩ mɩ-tɩ yɔ, ɩtɩŋna pʋ-yɔɔ nɛ ɛñazɩ tiŋ pe yaa isidi nabʋyʋ naa ndɩ ndɩ nɛ pɩla sʋlʋm kɩpam.
text_en: If you're feeling more adventurous, take the opportunity to juice or blend up some smoothies:

text: Pʋtɔmaa yɔ ɩtɩlɩɣ sʋlʋm nabʋyʋ kɛlɛʋ mbʋ ɩpɩzɩɣ ɩpuu nɛ tanaŋ tɛɛ sɔntɔ ɖeɖe pɩkɔŋ nɛ pɩmalɩnɩ-mɩ lɛ.
text_en: maybe you'll discover a simple beverage that you can make for breakfast when you're back to your daily routine.

text: Yee ɛcaɣ tɛtʋ sɔsɔtʊ taa ɖeŋdɖe sʋlʋm wɛ ndɩ yɔɔ yɔ, ɩwolo sʋlʋm faaɖɩ naa taa yaa ɖɩhɛzɩyɛ nɖɩ ɖɩwɛ haɖaa mpa pa-taa ɩɩtiiwoki yɔ.
text_en: If you live in a city with a varied drinking culture, go to bars or pubs in neighborhoods you don't frequent.

text: Mba paasɩŋ kʋdɔmɩŋ yaa fɛɖaa tɛ kʋnʋŋ yɔ, kʋdɔŋ kɩɖɛɖɛʊ nɛ ñɩŋgaaŋzɩ wɛna tɔbʋʋ nɩʋ camɩyɛ.
text_en: For those unfamiliar with medical jargon, the words infectious and contagious have distinct meanings.

text: Kʊdɔŋ kɩɖɛɛzʊʊ kɛ kʊdɔŋ ŋgʊ kɩlɩʊna mɩɩsʊ ɛzɩ viriisɩ , bakiteri , kpɛŋgbɛka yaa ɖalaa lɛla cɔlɔ
text_en: An infectious disease is one that is caused by a pathogen, such as a virus, bacterium, fungus or other parasites.

text: Kʋdɔŋ kɩɖɛdɩʋ kɛna kʋdɔŋ nŋgʋ kɩɖɛɣ kɛlɛʋ yee nɔɔyʋ ɛñɔtɩna kʋdɔndʋ yɔ.
text_en: A contagious disease is a disease which is easily transmitted by being in the vicinity of an infected person.

text: Kiwiyissi sakɩyɛ siki niye se paɖaa kʋdɔmɩŋ ndɩ ndɩ tɛ ɖatʋ kɛ manzʋʋ malɩɩ waa.
text_en: Many governments require visitors entering, or residents leaving, their countries to be vaccinated for a range of diseases.

text: Paɣtʊ ndʋ tɩbizʋ tɩtaɣna ajɛya wɛna a-tsa nɔmɔɖɔnʋ woba a-taa yaa ɛcal wobu a-taa yɔ.
text_en: These requirements may often depend on what countries a traveller has visited or intends to visit.

text: Charlɔtɩ, hayo yɔɔ Caroline taa ñʋʋ leleŋ kɛlɛ sɩ waŋ sakiyɛ pɩzɩɣ nɛ ana mpʋ añɩnɩɣ yɔ nɛ a-liu sɩ.
